items.title: Ordered monomial PBW basis for the shifted Yangian
items.statement:
For any fixed order on the shifted Drinfeld generators and on the root modes of
$Y_n(\sigma)$, their ordered monomials form a $\mathbb C$-basis of
$Y_n(\sigma)$. Its canonical associated graded algebra is the polynomial
algebra on the corresponding symbols, while its loop associated graded algebra
is the universal enveloping algebra of the current algebra
$\mathfrak{gl}_n[t](\sigma)$; the two graded algebras are different and
non-isomorphic in general. In the finite quotient $W(\lambda)$ the ordered
monomials in the finite Gauss range
$$s_{i,j}<r\le s_{i,j}+p_{\min(i,j)}$$
form a basis, and the commutative Kazhdan/canonical associated graded and the
noncommutative loop associated graded are distinct. Equivalently, the finite
$T$-coefficients with $s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}$ form an ordered PBW basis, where
$r$ is the unshifted coefficient index of $T=FDE$, not a reindexed value.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A shift matrix $\sigma$ attached to a pyramid with row lengths $0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n$, the shifted Yangian $Y_n(\sigma)$ with its generators and filtrations of [[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]], and the quotient $W(\lambda)=Y_n(\sigma)/(D_1^{(r)},r>p_1)$.

[F1] The RTT/Drinfeld presentation, the Gauss decomposition $T=FDE$, the two filtrations and the truncation are as in [[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]; the candidate finite index set to be established below is $s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}$ with $S_{i,j}=s_{i,j}+p_{\min(i,j)}$.

[F2] Ordered monomial PBW for enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional Lie algebras: an ordered monomial basis holds for $U(\mathfrak a)$ when $\mathfrak a$ is finite-dimensional ([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F3] The local Gan–Ginzburg transverse-product and Chevalley–Eilenberg lifting argument proves that the Kazhdan associated graded of the entire quantum Hamiltonian reduction is the polynomial coordinate algebra of the transverse slice. Its homogeneous coordinate degrees are $s_{i,j}+1,\ldots,s_{i,j}+\min(p_i,p_j)$ for each row pair; the doubled convention gives twice these degrees ([[lem-gan-ginzburg-skryabin-inputs-hold-for-the-type-a-pyramid-good-grading]], [[def-associated-graded-algebra-of-a-filtered-algebra]]).




## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The shifted Yangian generators and the finite quotient $W(\lambda)$.

1.1 **RTT spanning and the actual coproduct.** In the unshifted RTT algebra the commutator of modes $r,s$ has canonical degree at most $r+s-1$, so induction on total degree and the number of unordered pairs rewrites every word into ordered monomials. Matrix-unit brackets verify RTT for $L_a(u)=I+E^{(a)}/u$ in the $a$th factor of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_n)^{\otimes l}$. Multiplication of RTT matrices with commuting coefficient algebras preserves RTT: moving the two middle commuting tensor factors past each other allows the first RTT identity, then the second. Thus the iterated evaluation map is $T(u)\mapsto L_1(u)\cdots L_l(u)$. More generally shifted evaluation points give the ordered product $\prod_{a=1}^l(I+E^{(a)}/(u-c_a))$, in increasing factor order. Its $u^{-r}$ coefficient when all $c_a=0$ is $\sum_{a_1<\cdots<a_r}E^{(a_1)}\cdots E^{(a_r)}$, homogeneous of enveloping PBW degree $r$. [F1, F2, algebra, construct]

1.2 We first prove invariance of the actual path generators for both column arrangements, independently of generation. For a box a write c(a) for its column, $\rho_c=n-\sum_{d\ge c}q_d$ and $\widetilde E_{ab}=(-1)^{c(b)-c(a)}(E_{ab}+\delta_{ab}\rho_{c(a)})$. The negative PBW projection $\operatorname{pr}:U(\mathfrak g)=U(\mathfrak p)U(\mathfrak m)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ applies χ to the right factor. Its elementary rules are $\operatorname{pr}(ZB)=\chi(Z)B+\operatorname{pr}([Z,B])$ and $\operatorname{pr}(BZ)=B\chi(Z)$ for a negative matrix unit Z and a p-factor B. The bracket is $[\widetilde E_{ab},\widetilde E_{hk}]=\delta_{bh}(\widetilde E_{ak}-\delta_{ak}\rho_{c(a)})-\delta_{ak}(\widetilde E_{hb}-\delta_{hb}\rho_{c(b)})$, and $\chi(\widetilde E_{ab})=-\delta_{\operatorname{row}(a),\operatorname{row}(b)}$ at adjacent negative columns, zero at greater distance. The path sum $P_{ij;x}^{(r)}$ has total degree $\sum(c(b_t)-c(a_t)+1)=r$, p-factors, shared intervening rows, starting/ending rows i,j, strict forward joins when the intervening row exceeds x and weak reverse joins otherwise, and sign $(-1)^{r-s}$ times one minus for every intervening row at most x. Its ηtail image is the same path sum in the displayed shifted factors. Invariance means $\operatorname{pr}([z,\eta_{\rm tail}(P)])=0$. If an element B is invariant, then $(z-\chi(z))B=B(z-\chi(z))+[z,B]$ proves $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi B\subseteq U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$; hence invariant elements form a subalgebra, and products, commutators and coefficients of inverse series with identity constant are invariant. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 The local Gan–Ginzburg supplier is stated for the original left-justified diagram; we derive the reflected version by an actual graded Lie isomorphism. Let f reflect boxes, $\tau(E_{ab})=E'_{f(b),f(a)}$ reverse products, and let S on the reflected space be diagonal with $S_{bb}=(-1)^{\operatorname{col}'(b)}$. The linear map $\phi(x)=S(-\tau(x))S^{-1}$ is a Lie isomorphism, because $[\tau(x),\tau(y)]=-\tau([x,y])$. It preserves grading degrees, p and m, and the trace pairing. The diagonal-conjugation sign on every positive adjacent arrow is −1, so $\phi(e)=e'$ and $\chi'\phi=\chi$. It extends to an ALGEBRA isomorphism of enveloping algebras and takes $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ to $U(\mathfrak g')I_{\chi'}$. Thus it takes the entire untwisted left reduction $A=\eta_{\rm tail}(W)$ to $A'$: each defining commutator condition is equivalent under φ. The chart map is the explicit algebra isomorphism $\beta=\eta_{\rm tail}'^{-1}\phi\eta_{\rm tail}:W\to W'$. Scalar translations have smaller positive Kazhdan degree, so $\operatorname{gr}\beta=\operatorname{gr}\phi$. The doubled good grading, sl2 triple, trace-orthogonal slice and transverse product transport under φ. Consequently the proved original polynomial-slice and cohomological statements imply the reflected statements in its actual grading, including the homogeneous coordinate weights. The polynomial-slice part used here is choice-free; for consumers assuming AC as in the cohomological supplier, its left Skryabin quotient, local-nilpotence category, invariant space and equivalence maps also transport first through φ and then through β. This uses the original proved local supplier without enlarging its stated domain, and does not assert that a transpose subalgebra is the whole reflected reduction or that two chart twists act equally on a fixed module. [F1, F2, F3, construct, algebra]

1.4 **Index and inverse sign in the abstract quotient.** Write $A_i(u)=D_i(u)^{-1}=\sum_{t\ge0}A_i^{(t)}u^{-t}$, so $A_i^{(0)}=1$, while the defining relation uses $\widetilde D_i(u)=-A_i(u)$ with constant $-1$. Thus $[E_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)}]=-D_{i+1}^{(a+b-1)}-\sum_{t=1}^{a+b-1}A_i^{(t)}D_{i+1}^{(a+b-1-t)}$. Put $i=c-1$, $u=s_{c-1,c}$, $v=s_{c,c-1}$, $a=r-v$, $b=v+1$. Then $a+b-1=r$ and $D_c^{(r)}=-\sum_{t=1}^rA_{c-1}^{(t)}D_c^{(r-t)}-[E_{c-1}^{(r-v)},F_{c-1}^{(v+1)}]$. We use this only for $r>p_c=p_{c-1}+u+v$, so $a>p_{c-1}+u$ is an allowed but HIGH E mode, to be eliminated before the diagonal formula is used. Also $A_i^{(r)}=-\sum_{t=1}^rD_i^{(t)}A_i^{(r-t)}$, giving polynomial inverse coefficients with the same canonical degree bound. This derives the sign and indices, rather than treating a negative inverse as a positive one. [F1, algebra]

2.1 **Product Jacobian and independence.** Let $l$ be at least the largest coefficient index in a proposed relation. In the commutative symbol algebra of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_n)^{\otimes l}$ write $P_r(X_1,\ldots,X_l)=\sum_{a_1<\cdots<a_r}X_{a_1}\cdots X_{a_r}$. At $X_a=h_aI$, with nonzero pairwise distinct $h_a$, the differential on every matrix entry is $dP_r=\sum_a e_{r-1}(h_1,\ldots,\widehat{h_a},\ldots,h_l)dX_a$. The column coefficient polynomials $\prod_{b\ne a}(1+h_bz)$ are linearly independent, since evaluating at $z=-1/h_c$ leaves only column $c$, with a nonzero value. Hence the Jacobian is invertible. A polynomial relation of minimal total degree, differentiated and multiplied by the inverse Jacobian over the rational function field, makes each of its partial derivatives a lower-degree relation; minimality and characteristic zero force the relation to be constant and zero. Thus the coordinates $P_{r,ij}$, $1\le r\le l$, are algebraically independent. A highest weighted-degree part of an enveloping relation among their ordered lifts would contradict this polynomial independence by [F2]. This proves RTT PBW for all modes. The $h_a$ are scalar-matrix points in the symbol space, independently of spectral evaluation parameters. [F2, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

2.2 Group equal row lengths into the minimal admissible parabolic blocks ν, with final nonempty block m of size t. D/E/F below are its actual Gauss path coefficients. Deleting the last column embeds the smaller shifted matrix units into the current ones; on unshifted diagonal units this compensates the rho difference by a scalar translation, and on negative units it preserves χ. A dot denotes the smaller coefficients. With final column A, preceding column B, $L_{kj}=\widetilde E_{(A,k),(A,j)}$ and $C_{hj}=\widetilde E_{(B,h),(A,j)}$, the right end recursions, for any fixed bottom row h, are $D_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot D_{a;ij}^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m}(\sum_k\dot D_{a;ik}^{(r-1)}L_{kj}+[\dot D_{a;ih}^{(r-1)},C_{hj}])$, $E_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot E_{a;ij}^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m-1}(\sum_k\dot E_{a;ik}^{(r-1)}L_{kj}+[\dot E_{a;ih}^{(r-1)},C_{hj}])$, and $F_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot F_{a;ij}^{(r)}$. The E boundary formula is used for r>1. Deleting the FIRST column of the reflected arrangement has the ordinary embedding on the remaining shifted factors. With first column A, next B, $L_{ik}=\widetilde E_{(A,i),(A,k)}$ and $C_{ih}=\widetilde E_{(A,i),(B,h)}$, its LEFT recursions are $D_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot D_{a;ij}^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m}(\sum_kL_{ik}\dot D_{a;kj}^{(r-1)}+[C_{ih},\dot D_{a;hj}^{(r-1)}])$, $E_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot E_{a;ij}^{(r)}$, and $F_{a;ij}^{(r)}=\dot F_{a;ij}^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m-1}(\sum_kL_{ik}\dot F_{a;kj}^{(r-1)}+[C_{ih},\dot F_{a;hj}^{(r-1)}])$, with r>1 in the F boundary formula. To verify these identities, cut each path at its final or initial visit to the added column. Paths missing that column give the dotted coefficient; paths ending or starting in its block give the product sum. For a crossing path the two neighboring cut positions at the common bottom row h have opposite signs and give the two orders in the commutator; further visits pair by moving to the neighboring cut. The identical cut rule in a changed row interval proves the Gauss identities: paths without an intermediate visit occur once; paths with such a visit have the two neighboring cuts with opposite sign. Thus these are identities for the actual Gauss coefficients. In particular LEFT deletion corrects F and leaves E unchanged; it does not use the interchanged E/F display in the source. [F1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

2.3 **Finite spanning: earlier blocks and boundary E/F.** In the abstract quotient by $D_1^{(r)}$, $r>p_1$, let $\Omega_c$ contain D modes $1\le a\le c$, $1\le r\le p_a$, E roots $a<b\le c$, $s_{ab}<r\le s_{ab}+p_a$, and F roots $a<b\le c$, $s_{ba}<r\le s_{ba}+p_a$; let $B_c$ be their algebra. Induct on c to show every allowed mode with endpoints at most c belongs to $B_c$ with total canonical degree at most its index. The case c=1 is the imposed truncation, including $p_1=0$. For the inductive step put $u=s_{c-1,c}$ and $v=s_{c,c-1}$. For $r>u+p_{c-1}$, the D–E relation gives $E_{c-1}^{(r)}=[D_{c-1}^{(r-u)},E_{c-1}^{(u+1)}]-\sum_{t=1}^{r-u-1}D_{c-1}^{(t)}E_{c-1}^{(r-t)}$. Replace every earlier D by its block-inductive finite expression and expand its commutator by Leibniz. The bracket of an earlier finite diagonal mode of index a with the lowest boundary E gives terms $D^{(t)}E_{c-1}^{(a+u-t)}$ with $a\le p_{c-1}$ in the only nonzero diagonal block, hence new E indices at most $u+p_{c-1}$. An earlier finite root $E_{b,c-1}^{(a)}$ gives $E_{b,c}^{(a+u)}$ and any block-refinement split terms, all with $a+u\le s_{b,c-1}+p_b+u=s_{b,c}+p_b$. Earlier negative roots and earlier positive roots without endpoint $c-1$ commute with the lowest boundary E. Thus the expanded commutator is in $B_c$. In the sum $u+1\le r-t<r$, so induction on r reduces those E modes; all products have degree at most r. The reversed D–F relation and reversed product orders give the same argument with boundary bound $v+p_{c-1}$. [F1, step 1.4, algebra]

3.1 **Gauss and shifted PBW.** Coefficientwise formal inversion and $T=FDE$ give mutually inverse polynomial changes between RTT and Gauss coordinates: the Gauss mode of index $r$ equals the corresponding RTT coordinate plus expressions in smaller mode indices of total canonical degree $r$. Consequently the canonical symbols of all Gauss root modes are a polynomial coordinate system. The shifted Drinfeld relations straighten shifted root-mode words, with lower canonical-degree commutator corrections; the adjacent root commutator definitions and Serre relations perform the higher-root straightening. Their RTT images have the same Gauss symbols in the allowed shifted ranges. Those symbols form an independent subset of the polynomial coordinate system, so these spanning words are independent and the shifted presentation embeds. Thus its canonical associated graded is precisely the polynomial algebra on its allowed root symbols. This argument concerns the untruncated algebra; it does not infer independence after quotienting. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 Induct on the number of columns, deleting the last column in the original left-justified diagram and the first in the reflected diagram. A one-column diagram has no negative algebra, so every mode is invariant. Empty rows have only formal constants and zero positive coefficients. All earlier D blocks, all nonboundary E/F blocks, and F in right deletion or E in left deletion are unchanged by step 2.2. Their path monomials have no forbidden preceding-bottom target in right deletion, or following-bottom source in left deletion; commuting a new negative into such a monomial produces a negative unit of greater column distance with zero χ, and moving it to the right keeps this absent endpoint. Thus their projected brackets vanish. Induction supplies old-negative invariance of every dotted coefficient. The old negative algebra commutes with L and C in step 2.2, so its character ideal is preserved by those factors, proving old-negative invariance of the changed coefficients. The complete negative Lie algebra is generated by the old one and the new adjacent-column matrices: brackets through a row present in intervening bottom rows produce each longer negative matrix. Jacobi and the normalizer identity in step 1.2 propagate invariance from these generators. Only the new adjacent matrices need be checked below. [step 1.2, step 2.2, algebra]

3.3 **Higher roots and the final diagonal elimination.** For $b<c-1$, the defining root recursions are $E_{b,c}^{(r)}=[E_{b,c-1}^{(r-u)},E_{c-1}^{(u+1)}]$ and $F_{c,b}^{(r)}=[F_{c-1}^{(v+1)},F_{c-1,b}^{(r-v)}]$. Reduce the earlier endpoint factors by the c−1 hypothesis; the same Leibniz bounds in step 2.3 place every new root in $B_c$, including high modes, using the finite allowed new roots in $\Omega_c$. Now use step 1.4 for $D_c^{(r)}$, $r>p_c$. Every inverse earlier coefficient is in $B_{c-1}$ and every $D_c^{(r-t)}$ has smaller index, so induction on r treats its sum. First replace the upper $E_{c-1}^{(r-v)}$ by the finite expression just constructed, then expand the bracket with the lowest boundary F. Earlier D/F factors give bounded new F roots and earlier factors; earlier E factors commute with that boundary F. A finite new E root starting at c−1 has index $a\le u+p_{c-1}$, so its E–F convolution has only $D_c$ indices at most $a+v\le p_c$. A new E root starting at b<c−1 gives earlier-endpoint roots and earlier factors, reduced by the block hypothesis, and cannot create a high $D_c$ mode. Thus this commutator uses only $D_c$ indices at most $p_c$, and the induction closes with the asserted degree control. In particular higher diagonal modes are polynomial expressions, not zero modes. [F1, step 1.4, step 2.3, algebra]

4.1 The changed D^(1) is a sum of the row-pair diagonal-column blocks; its two adjacent-column projected commutators cancel. Let the neighboring column have height u≥t, with b=u−t shorter rows and cutoff x=n−t. In RIGHT deletion put $z=\widetilde E_{(A,f),(B,g)}$, f bottom and g arbitrary. In D^(2), and in boundary E^(2) when the shift is1, the single bridge contributes scalar $-u\delta_{gi}\delta_{fj}$. The bottom plus paths $\sum_kB_{ik}A_{kj}$ contribute $+t\delta_{gi}\delta_{fj}$ and matrix terms $-\delta_{gi}A_{fj}+\delta_{fj}B_{ig}$ for g bottom. The shorter minus paths in B contribute $+b\delta_{gi}\delta_{fj}$ and $+\delta_{fj}B_{ig}$ for g shorter. Moving their negative factor through the following block yields one additional χ correction for each shorter row; this is the scalar b term. The single bridge gives the negative of all the matrix terms, and $-u+t+b=0$. In LEFT deletion put $z=\widetilde E_{(B,f),(A,g)}$, f arbitrary and g bottom. The bridge scalar is $-t\delta_{gi}\delta_{fj}$; bottom plus paths $\sum_kA_{ik}B_{kj}$ give $+t\delta_{gi}\delta_{fj}$ and $-\delta_{gi}B_{fj}+\delta_{fj}A_{ig}$ for f bottom. Shorter minus paths $-\sum_hB_{ih}B_{hj}$ give $-\delta_{gi}B_{fj}$ for f shorter and NO scalar: the extra negative χ involves a shorter row h and bottom row g. The bridge has the opposite matrix terms. Therefore $-t+t=0$ and all matrices cancel, for D^(2) and boundary F^(2). Paths outside these adjacent columns have zero projection by the support argument in step 3.2. This proves the exact jump-one base cases in both actual LEFT reductions. [step 1.2, step 2.2, step 3.2, algebra]

4.2 For a larger boundary shift, or a rectangle, the first two end columns have equal height t. A double dot deletes both and $K_{s;ij}=\ddot D_{m;ij}^{(s)}$; replacing K with the corresponding boundary $\ddot E$ in RIGHT deletion or $\ddot F$ in LEFT deletion gives the same calculation. In RIGHT deletion call the last positions C,B,A, and write $B_{ck}=\widetilde E_{(B,c),(B,k)}$, $A_{kj}=\widetilde E_{(A,k),(A,j)}$, $C_{hk}=\widetilde E_{(C,h),(B,k)}$, $J_{cj}=\widetilde E_{(B,c),(A,j)}$ and $H_{hj}=\widetilde E_{(C,h),(A,j)}$. Twice expanding step 2.2 expresses the changed r-mode as the sum of eight groups $A_0=K_{r;ij}$, $B_0=\sum_cK_{r-1;ic}B_{cj}$, $C_0=[K_{r-1;ih},C_{hj}]$, $D_0=\sum_kK_{r-1;ik}A_{kj}$, $E_0=\sum_{k,c}K_{r-2;ic}B_{ck}A_{kj}$, $F_0=\sum_k[K_{r-2;ih},C_{hk}]A_{kj}$, $G_0=\sum_cK_{r-2;ic}J_{cj}$, $H_0=[K_{r-2;ih},H_{hj}]$. For $z=\widetilde E_{(A,f),(B,g)}$ their projected brackets, in that order, are $0,-\delta_{fj}K_{r-1;ig},0,+\delta_{fj}K_{r-1;ig},R,S,-R,-S$, where $R=t\delta_{fj}K_{r-2;ig}-K_{r-2;ig}A_{fj}+\delta_{fj}\sum_cK_{r-2;ic}B_{cg}$ and $S=\delta_{fj}[K_{r-2;ih},C_{hg}]$. The bracket in step 1.2 proves this table by moving each negative factor to the RIGHT. The t summation rows give the scalar in R; the bridge J gives its opposite because $\rho_A-\rho_B=t$. K lies in the twice-deleted p and commutes with z. The eight expressions cancel for EVERY r>1. [step 1.2, step 2.2, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 At a RIGHT jump-one boundary, for a fixed earlier-block row g and r>1 the coefficient recursions in U(p) are $D_{m;ij}^{(r+1)}=[F_{m-1;ig}^{(2)},E_{m-1;gj}^{(r)}]+\sum_{s=0}^r\widetilde D_{m-1;gg}^{(r+1-s)}D_{m;ij}^{(s)}$ and $E_{m-1;ij}^{(r+1)}=[D_{m-1;ig}^{(2)},E_{m-1;gj}^{(r)}]-\sum_fD_{m-1;if}^{(1)}E_{m-1;fj}^{(r)}$. Here $\widetilde D(u)=-D(u)^{-1}$, with order-zero coefficient −I. The corresponding LEFT identities are $D_{m;ij}^{(r+1)}=[F_{m-1;ig}^{(r)},E_{m-1;gj}^{(2)}]+\sum_{s=0}^rD_{m;ij}^{(s)}\widetilde D_{m-1;gg}^{(r+1-s)}$ and $F_{m-1;ij}^{(r+1)}=[F_{m-1;ig}^{(r)},D_{m-1;gj}^{(2)}]-\sum_fF_{m-1;if}^{(r)}D_{m-1;fj}^{(1)}$. These are algebraic coefficient identities, independent of invariance and generation. Expanding the E identity by the right end recursion gives $\dot E^{(r+1)}+\sum\dot D^{(1)}\dot E^{(r)}$, its product with L, and its commutator with C; collecting with step 2.2 gives $E^{(r+1)}+\sum D^{(1)}E^{(r)}$. The left F expansion instead gives $\dot F^{(r+1)}+\sum\dot F^{(r)}\dot D^{(1)}$, its LEFT product with L and $[C,\,\cdot\,]$, which collect to $F^{(r+1)}+\sum F^{(r)}D^{(1)}$. The unchanged earlier D^(2) has no boundary endpoint and commutes with L,C. Expanding the boundary E–F bracket similarly gives the D identity: the coefficient convolution $D\widetilde D=-I$ cancels paired split paths with opposite cut signs, leaving the changed D coefficient. Thus the recursions hold in both product orders. Every earlier D/inverse-D coefficient and the unaffected E or F coefficient is invariant by step 3.2; the changed base coefficients are invariant by step 4.1. Since the sum uses s≤r, induction on r proves invariance of ALL changed jump-one modes. [step 1.2, step 2.2, step 3.2, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 The REFLECTED calculation is a direct LEFT-ideal calculation, not an anti-map reversal of step 4.2. Call its first positions A,B,C, and write $L_{ik}=\widetilde E_{(A,i),(A,k)}$, $B_{kc}=\widetilde E_{(B,k),(B,c)}$, $C_{kh}=\widetilde E_{(B,k),(C,h)}$, $J_{ic}=\widetilde E_{(A,i),(B,c)}$, $H_{ih}=\widetilde E_{(A,i),(C,h)}$. The eight groups are $A_0=K_{r;ij}$, $B_0=\sum_kB_{ik}K_{r-1;kj}$, $C_0=[C_{ih},K_{r-1;hj}]$, $D_0=\sum_kL_{ik}K_{r-1;kj}$, $E_0=\sum_{k,c}L_{ik}B_{kc}K_{r-2;cj}$, $F_0=\sum_kL_{ik}[C_{kh},K_{r-2;hj}]$, $G_0=\sum_cJ_{ic}K_{r-2;cj}$, $H_0=[H_{ih},K_{r-2;hj}]$. For $z=\widetilde E_{(B,f),(A,g)}$ their projected brackets are $0,+\delta_{ig}K_{r-1;fj},0,-\delta_{ig}K_{r-1;fj},R',S',-R',-S'$, with $R'=t\delta_{ig}K_{r-2;fj}-\delta_{ig}\sum_cB_{fc}K_{r-2;cj}+L_{ig}K_{r-2;fj}$ and $S'=-\delta_{ig}[C_{fh},K_{r-2;hj}]$. For example $[z,L_{ik}]=\delta_{gi}\widetilde E_{(B,f),(A,k)}$, and moving this negative through B gives $-\delta_{fk}B_{kc}+\delta_{fc}$; summing k gives the t term. The other part of the product bracket gives the L term. The bridge J has the opposite matrix terms and scalar $\rho_A-\rho_B=-t$; the F/H terms cancel because $[z,H_{ih}]=\delta_{gi}C_{fh}$ and z commutes with K. Thus every group is accounted for and cancels in the reflected LEFT reduction for EVERY r>1. If there are only two columns, K has only its formal constant coefficients and terms involving the third column vanish, so the same table applies. [step 1.2, step 2.2, step 3.2, algebra]

6.1 Steps 3.2, 4.1, 5.1, 4.2 and 5.2 cover every allowed parabolic D/E/F mode for the original and reflected arrangements. Refining a minimal block is its formal Gauss decomposition: coefficients of its inverse and resulting factors are polynomials in its previous coefficients, hence invariant by step 1.2. This gives all ordinary simple modes; higher-root commutator definitions give all higher roots. Therefore the actual untwisted-chart images $P_{ii;i-1}^{(r)},P_{i,i+1;i}^{(r)},P_{i+1,i;i}^{(r)}$ and all their higher-root polynomials belong to their actual left reductions. This conclusion covers the infinite allowed mode families and does not rely on finite generation, finite truncation or a reflected W identification. [step 1.2, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 4.2, step 5.2, algebra]

7.1 **Finite Levi Jacobian.** Project $U(\mathfrak p)$ to its column Levi enveloping algebra and take canonical symbols. At its diagonal point $X_c=h_cI$, let $Q_i(z)=\prod_{c\le p_i}(1+h_cz)$. The diagonal D first variations are $z\prod_{a\le p_i,a\ne c}(1+h_az)$. For $i<j$, set $m=p_i$, $M=p_j$. A first variation in a common column $c\le m$ has just one off-diagonal factor. Summing the same-column negative-cut repeats and the strictly increasing positive-cut visits in the path formula gives $dE_{ij}(z)=z\prod_{a=m+1}^M(1+h_az)/(1+h_cz)$ and $dF_{ji}(z)=z/(1+h_cz)$ on that entry. These are identities for the allowed coefficient derivatives, not an identification of excluded low product coefficients with shifted generators. Their coefficients in modes $M-m+k$ and $k$, $1\le k\le m$, are respectively $(-h_c)^{k-1}\prod_{a=m+1}^M(h_a-h_c)$ and $(-h_c)^{k-1}$. For higher roots, the canonical symbol of the adjacent root commutator is the Levi Lie–Poisson bracket. At $X_c=h_cI$ this Poisson tensor is zero, so the differential of a bracket uses only the two first differentials and the differential of the Poisson tensor. With $i<k<j$ and $p_k=t$, the coefficients from $E_{ik}^{(r-s_{kj})}$ and $E_{kj}^{(s_{kj}+1)}$ multiply to $(-h_c)^{a-1}\prod_{m<b\le t}(h_b-h_c)\prod_{t<b\le M}(h_b-h_c)$ when $r=M-m+a$, since $\{X_{c,ik},X_{c,kj}\}=X_{c,ij}$. For F the reversed recursion uses $\{X_{c,jk},X_{c,ki}\}=X_{c,ji}$, with coefficients one and $(-h_c)^{r-1}$. Thus induction gives the displayed first variations for all higher roots as well. Choose the $h_c$ nonzero and pairwise distinct. Each row-pair block is Vandermonde with nonzero column factors; each diagonal block is the elementary-symmetric Jacobian from step 2.1. Different row pairs use disjoint entry variables, so the full Jacobian has rank $\sum_{ij}\min(p_i,p_j)$. The corresponding finite symbols are algebraically independent by step 2.1's differentiation argument. Reflection reverses column order and interchanges E and F, giving the same invertible blocks with transposed shifts. Empty rows contribute zero-sized blocks. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 **The whole reduction is generated.** Write $\mathcal W$ for the entire quantum Hamiltonian reduction, before any identification with a Yangian quotient. By [F3] its homogeneous Hilbert series is $H(t)=\prod_{i,j}\prod_{r=s_{ij}+1}^{s_{ij}+\min(p_i,p_j)}(1-t^r)^{-1}$. Each weight is positive, so every coefficient is finite. Step 6.1 places every ordered finite-generator monomial of total degree at most $d$ inside $F_d^K\mathcal W$. Step 7.1 and enveloping PBW make these monomials independent: a highest-degree relation after Levi projection would give a polynomial relation among the independent symbols. Their number is exactly $\sum_{k\le d}[t^k]H(t)$, which is also $\dim F_d^K\mathcal W$ by [F3] for the original pair and step 1.3 for the reflected pair. Thus their span equals $F_d^K\mathcal W$ for every $d$. Exhaustivity proves generation of the entire reduction and its ordered filtered basis, and also injectivity of the Levi projection on that entire algebra. The same homogeneous dimension equality proves full generation for the reflected reduction using its own allowed modes and transposed shifts. This uses the Gan–Ginzburg slice theorem independently of W-PBW, not just generic independence in a restricted subalgebra. [F2, F3, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 1.3, algebra]

9.1 **Relations, finite order and the whole-algebra identification.** The end path identities prove the shifted coefficient relations and the $D_1$ cutoff on the invariant representatives. One can check them after Levi projection, now injective on the entire reduction by step 8.1: the right end images are $D_a^{(r)}\mapsto\dot D_a^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m}\sum_k\dot D_{a;ik}^{(r-1)}L_{kj}$, $E_a^{(r)}\mapsto\dot E_a^{(r)}+\delta_{a,m-1}\sum_k\dot E_{a;ik}^{(r-1)}L_{kj}$, and $F_a^{(r)}\mapsto\dot F_a^{(r)}$; the left versions place L before the dotted coefficients and correct F instead. Substitute these finite coefficient expressions in each D–D, D–E, D–F, E–F, equal-root and adjacent-root relation. Terms with no L give the smaller relation. Terms with one L give the smaller D-weight relation; terms with two L use $[L_{ij},L_{hk}]=\delta_{jh}L_{ik}-\delta_{ki}L_{hj}$. The inverse-D convolution cancels paired split coefficients, and the adjacent triple relations group into those same terms and the matrix Jacobi identity. Hence the relations hold by column induction, starting with matrix-unit brackets at one column; injectivity lifts them back to the actual reduction. For D1 the cutoff row interval is empty, so every join is strictly forward; a path beginning and ending in row1 satisfies $r=\sum(c(b_t)-c(a_t)+1)\le c(b_s)-c(a_1)+1\le p_1$. Thus the smallest-row path has no coefficient above $p_1$, giving the actual $D_1$ cutoff in either arrangement. There is therefore a homomorphism from the abstract truncated quotient onto the invariant-generated whole algebra. Steps 2.3 and 3.3 give finite spanning; commutator swapping lowers canonical degree, so induction on that degree and the number of unordered pairs straightens these finite expressions into ordered $\Omega_n$ monomials. Their images are the independent ordered reduction basis of step 8.1, so the homomorphism is injective as well. This proves the quotient presentation and the finite Gauss PBW basis without restricting an infinite basis through a quotient. [F1, F2, step 2.2, step 6.1, step 8.1, step 2.3, step 3.3, algebra]

9.2 The full generator theorem just proved for BOTH arrangements now identifies the original head/right model. With the reflected-box anti-map τ from step 1.3, send a path $(a_1,b_1),\ldots,(a_s,b_s)$ to $(f(b_s),f(a_s)),\ldots,(f(b_1),f(a_1))$. Each displacement is unchanged. A reversed join compares $l+1-c(a_{k+1})$ with $l+1-c(b_k)$, so its strict-forward or weak-reverse rule is exactly the original one; its row is $\operatorname{row}(a_{k+1})=\operatorname{row}(b_k)$, preserving its sign. Total degree, number of factors and total sign are identical; the product order is precisely τ's reversal. This involutive bijection proves $\tau(P_{ij;x}^{(r)})=P_{ji;x}^{\prime(r)}$ for ALL i,j,x and modes r, including the diagonal constants at r=0. In particular τ exchanges simple E/F images and fixes the corresponding D images, transposing the shift matrix and preserving mode number. Since these explicit images generate each WHOLE reduction by step 8.1, both inclusions give $\tau(W)=W'$, rather than only the image of a path subalgebra. [step 6.1, step 1.3, step 8.1, construct, algebra]

10.1 The preceding construction applies to both directional shift matrices, using the corresponding left or right end formulas in step 9.1. Thus it proves the full finite quotient basis, equality with the whole reduction, and strict canonical/Kazhdan filtration in both arrangements. Its degree-r homogeneous basis is the monomial basis counted by the exact slice Hilbert series, and the projection used for the relation check is injective on the entire reduction. These are the prerequisites for the original right-normalizer identification below. [step 1.3, step 8.1, step 9.1, algebra]

10.2 **Actual original prefix coefficient identity.** Let $\lambda_m$ be the first m columns of the decreasing-column pyramid, $I=I_{m-1}:U(\mathfrak g_{m-1})\hookrightarrow U(\mathfrak g_m)$ the ordinary UNSHIFTED box embedding, and $b_a(j)$ the box in row j and column a when it exists. Put negative-index coefficients zero and $T_{ij}^{(0)}=\delta_{ij}$. The original coefficient recursion, for r>0, is $T_{ij}^{(r)}(\lambda_m)=I(T_{ij}^{(r)})-\sum_{h\le n-q_m,\ s_{hj}\le r}I(T_{ih}^{(r-s_{hj})})I(T_{hj}^{(s_{hj})})+\sum_{h>n-q_m}I(T_{ih}^{(r-1)})E_{b_m(h),b_m(j)}-[I(T_{ij}^{(r-1)}),E_{b_{m-1}(j),b_m(j)}]$, where coefficients inside I belong to $\lambda_{m-1}$ and shifts in the sum belong to $\lambda_m$. The final THREE terms are omitted for $j\le n-q_m$, and a nonexistent box omits its term. To derive the identity before any cutoff is known, apply the right end identities to the last Gauss block in the ordinary chart. D has its smaller D plus its last-column Levi product and minus its previous-to-last bridge commutator; E has the same two corrections and starts with the smaller $\bar E$. The precise smaller-block subtraction is $\bar E_{a,b}(u)=E_{a,b}(u)-\sum_{c=a}^{b-1}E_{a,c}(u)E_{c,b}^{(\dot s_{cb}+1)}u^{-\dot s_{cb}-1}$, all in the smaller diagram. For a shorter block c and last block b, $\dot s_{cb}+1=s_{cb}$. Insert these expressions into $T_{ij}(u)=\sum(F_{c,a}(u)D_c(u)E_{c,b}(u))_{ij}$. Unchanged terms give the first embedded T; the $\bar E$ subtractions group by shorter terminal row h into the product with split $(r-s_{hj},s_{hj})$; the L products group into the Levi sum. Leibniz groups the common bridge into the displayed single commutator. Higher-root end identities follow by their adjacent recursion; its earlier-block factor has no terminal bridge endpoint, so its bracket with that bridge is zero. This proves the prefix identity itself and retains its actual coefficient index. [F1, step 2.2, step 9.1, algebra, construct]

11.1 **Loop symbols and the two graded algebras.** In the unshifted RTT relation the top loop-degree commutator is the current matrix-unit bracket; terms with two positive-index factors have smaller loop degree. Gauss multiplication changes a mode of index $r$ by products of at least two factors of total canonical index $r$, hence smaller loop degree than $r-1$. Taking the shifted root relations gives the same brackets with allowed current modes $e_{ij}t^a$, $a\ge s_{ij}$; shift additivity makes their span a Lie subalgebra. The ordered basis of step 3.1 is a filtered basis also for intrinsic loop degree, because loop straightening never raises total degree and independence of the full ordered words rules out a lower-degree expression. Current PBW uses only finite-dimensional PBW: any proposed relation uses finitely many modes, and a jet quotient with larger cutoff preserves those basis vectors and makes their enveloping monomials independent. Hence the loop associated graded is $U(\mathfrak{gl}_n[t](\sigma))$. Canonical degree instead gave a commutative polynomial algebra. For the finite reduction the Kazhdan associated graded is the commutative slice algebra from step 8.1, while the leading single-factor terms of the finite generators lie in the actual centralizer $\mathfrak g^e\subseteq\mathfrak p$; the next theorem identifies the loop graded algebra by ambient enveloping PBW. Noncommutativity distinguishes the two graded algebras whenever the corresponding Lie algebra is nonabelian. [F1, F2, F3, step 3.1, step 8.1, step 10.1, algebra]

11.2 **Every coefficient above the bound is zero.** For the original decreasing-column diagram $S_{ij}=s_{ij}+\min(p_i,p_j)=p_j$ for EVERY ordered row pair. Induct on the column count m using step 10.2; the one-column T has no coefficient above one directly. An empty row contributes only a diagonal constant. If $j\le n-q_m$, its row length is unchanged on removal, so the only embedded T term vanishes for $r>p_j$ by induction. If j is a bottom row, $p_j=m$, and the first embedded T vanishes for $r>m$ because its smaller target-row length is m−1. In each shorter-row product, $p_h$ is unchanged and $s_{hj}=m-p_h$, so $r-s_{hj}>p_h=S_{ih}(\lambda_{m-1})$ for ANY i, killing its first factor. In the Levi sum every h has smaller row length m−1, and $r-1>m-1=S_{ih}(\lambda_{m-1})$ kills its coefficient. The same inequality kills the T coefficient inside the final commutator. This covers every term, including the boundary $r=m+1$, and proves $T_{ij}^{(r)}=0$ for $r>S_{ij}$. The lower zero range $0<r\le s_{ij}$ follows coefficientwise from FDE and shift additivity. No truncation fact was assumed to prove itself. [F1, step 10.2, algebra]

12.1 **Finite T coordinates and loop symbols.** Coefficientwise FDE and Gauss inversion are weighted triangular in the original index r: the mode equals its corresponding Gauss coordinate plus products of smaller mode indices of total canonical degree r. The finite Gauss eliminations from steps 2.3 and 3.3 and the actual cutoff in step 11.2 close both inversions on exactly the finite set. Thus these finite canonical symbols are another polynomial coordinate system, and the ordered finite T monomials have the same filtered basis as the Gauss monomials in step 9.1, in any prescribed order. A signed path term with k factors and coefficient index r has ambient good degree at most r−k; scalar replacements lower it further. Only its single-factor part contributes in degree r−1, giving $(-1)^{r-1}\sum_{\operatorname{row}(a)=i,\operatorname{row}(b)=j,\ c(b)-c(a)=r-1}E_{ab}=(-1)^{r-1}e_{ij;r-1}$. Products introduced by Gauss inversion have at least two factors and smaller good degree. This proves the symbol dictionary with the existing coefficient index and no spectral rescaling. [F1, step 3.3, step 9.1, step 11.2, algebra]

12.2 Put $\eta_{\rm head}(E_{ab})=E_{ab}+\delta_{ab}(n-\sum_{d\le c(a)}q_d)$. This and ηtail are algebra automorphisms: a matrix bracket can have diagonal part only from $E_{ab},E_{ba}\in\mathfrak p$, which forces equal columns and equal diagonal shifts, so the scalar functional kills the commutator; the negative scalar translation is the inverse. Reflection gives $\sum_{d\ge c'(f(a))}q'_d=\sum_{d\le c(a)}q_d$, hence $\tau\eta_{\rm head}=\eta'_{\rm tail}\tau$. Also $\tau(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m'$, $\chi'\tau=\chi$ by the trace calculation, and $\tau(I_\chi U(\mathfrak g))=U(\mathfrak g')I_{\chi'}$, since τ reverses products and sends each shifted negative generator to its reflected one. Therefore $\tau([\eta_{\rm head}(u),x])=[\tau(x),\eta'_{\rm tail}(\tau(u))]$. Bijectivity shows that u satisfies the ORIGINAL head/right condition exactly when τ(u) belongs to the reflected LEFT reduction. Step 9.2 identifies its inverse image with the original W, proving BOTH inclusions in $W=\{u:[\eta_{\rm head}(u),\mathfrak m]\subseteq I_\chi U(\mathfrak g)\}$. The induced Gauss transpose also satisfies $\tau(T_{ij}^{(r)})=T_{ji}^{\prime(r)}$: apply the coefficientwise reversed FDE factors and their Gauss cut identities. Thus step 11.2 gives the reflected upper cutoff $r>S_{ji}=S_{ij}^{\prime}$, with the same finite triangular T basis. This proves right invariance for every original shifted generator, higher-root mode and product, beyond the numerical identity $\eta_{\rm head}-\eta_{\rm tail}=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak m}\operatorname{ad}$. [step 9.2, algebra]

13.1 Write $J_L=U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ and $J_R=I_\chi U(\mathfrak g)$. The identities $(x-\chi(x))\eta_{\rm tail}(w)=\eta_{\rm tail}(w)(x-\chi(x))+[x,\eta_{\rm tail}(w)]$ and $\eta_{\rm head}(w)(x-\chi(x))=(x-\chi(x))\eta_{\rm head}(w)+[\eta_{\rm head}(w),x]$ prove $J_L\eta_{\rm tail}(w)\subseteq J_L$ and $\eta_{\rm head}(w)J_R\subseteq J_R$ for every w∈W. Thus $Q_L=U(\mathfrak g)/J_L$ has its actual right action $\overline a\cdot w=\overline{a\eta_{\rm tail}(w)}$, and $Q_R=U(\mathfrak g)/J_R$ its actual left action $w\cdot\overline a=\overline{\eta_{\rm head}(w)a}$, commuting with the respective enveloping actions by associativity. These are module quotients, not quotient rings. Right Whittaker vectors act by $v\cdot w=v\eta_{\rm head}(w)$ because they annihilate J_R. Turning a right U(g)-module into a left reflected module by $a'v=v\tau^{-1}(a')$ identifies its right Whittaker space and W action with the reflected left ones, using $\tau^{-1}\eta'_{\rm tail}\tau=\eta_{\rm head}$. For consumers assuming AC, transporting their proved left Skryabin equivalence through the reflected Lie isomorphism in step 1.3 and then this anti-map gives the right equivalence with inverse $-\otimes_WQ_R$; that conditional categorical assertion is separate from the choice-free algebra identity. Every action is the explicit original or reflected chart action; no equality of different twists on an arbitrary fixed representation is assumed. [step 1.3, step 12.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The independence argument is a finite-dimensional PBW argument in disguise: any finite relation involves finitely many modes, and mapping the corresponding finitely many generators to a jet Lie algebra makes their PBW images independent. No PBW theorem for the infinite-dimensional current algebra is assumed.

- The two related graded algebras are a recurring source of errors: the symbolic degrees of the Kazhdan filtration are the coordinates of the Slodowy slice, while the loop degrees are current-algebra degrees; the double centralizer arguments on this page use the loop filtration.

items.title: Skryabin's equivalence for the type-A Whittaker pair
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], inherited from assertion (2) of the good-grading cohomology supplier.

Let $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$, $W(\lambda)$,
$Q_\chi$ and $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ be as in
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Then the functor
$$Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$$
is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor
$\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor
$?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the
exact functor
$$M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}\bigl((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X\bigr)$$
on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a
$W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map
$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$
is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms
$(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible,
and for the one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting
isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$
is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The pyramid data, the bimodule $Q_\chi$ and the Whittaker category of [[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]], and a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$. Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the arbitrary-module equivalence and transported tensor assertions.

[F1] For every $W(\lambda)$-module $M$, the twisted $\mathfrak m$-cohomology of $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M$ vanishes in positive degrees and its degree-zero part is $M$; for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the invariants detect vanishing ([[lem-gan-ginzburg-skryabin-inputs-hold-for-the-type-a-pyramid-good-grading]]).

[F2] $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a $(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule, and tensoring the canonical element $1_\chi$ with a $W(\lambda)$-module gives a left adjoint to $\mathrm{Wh}$; the unit and counit are the natural maps $M\to\mathrm{Wh}(Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)$, $v\mapsto1_\chi\otimes v$ and $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}\mathrm{Wh}(M)\to M$, $u1_\chi\otimes v\mapsto uv$ ([[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]], [[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F3] Chevalley-Eilenberg exactness: tensoring with a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module preserves the Whittaker category and is exact, and the long exact cohomology sequence computes the cohomology of extensions ([[def-chevalley-eilenberg-cochains]], [[thm-long-exact-sequence-in-lie-algebra-cohomology]]).

[F4] The loop-symbol computation: in PBW degree the leading system of the $\chi$-equations for the tensor identification is polynomial Taylor translation on $\mathbb C[M_{\mathrm{unip}}]$ with invertible constant term; the finite matrices $X,Y$ constructed from the prefix-$T$ formulas are inverse by degree recursion, and the coefficient index is the actual displacement $\mathrm{col}(a)-\mathrm{col}(b)$ with no $u^s$ reindexing ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], [[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The bimodule $Q_\chi$, a $W(\lambda)$-module $M$, a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, and the maps $\mu_{M,X}$; assume AC as specified above.

1.1 Unit and counit. The adjunction between $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-$ and $\mathrm{Wh}$ has the unit $u_M\colon M\to\mathrm{Wh}(Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)$ and counit $c_M\colon Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}\mathrm{Wh}(M)\to M$ of [F2]. For every $M$, the kernel and cokernel of $u_M$ and $c_M$ lie in the kernel of the invariants functor: applying $H^0$ to the unit and using the vanishing of [F1] identifies the composite with the identity; a short exact sequence argument with the long exact sequence of [F3] then shows that if $H^0$ of a map in the category is an isomorphism then the map is an isomorphism, since the kernel and cokernel have vanishing invariants and a nonzero object of the category has nonzero invariants by [F1]. Hence $u_M,c_M$ are isomorphisms and the two functors are quasi-inverse. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 Exactness and detection. Exactness of $\mathrm{Wh}$ follows because it is inverse to the exact functor $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-$ (tensoring with the right flat module $Q_\chi$, whose flatness is part of the free right-module structure of the source), and the detection statement is the case $H^0=0$ of [F1]. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 The transported tensor functor. For $M\in W(\lambda)$-mod and finite-dimensional $X$, the functor $M\mapsto\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X)$ is exact in $M$ because the composed functors are exact; it is the transport of $?\otimes X$ across the equivalence. [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Triangularity of the displayed tensor map.** Keep the polynomial-coordinate/distribution pairing from the good-grading calculation: the right-free PBW coordinates identify $Q_\chi\otimes_W M$ with the locally nilpotent coinduced model, by finite weighted Taylor pairing and descending leading-term subtraction, followed by filtered unions. Cofree evaluation on Whittaker vectors of this model tensored with $X$ gives a vector-space isomorphism $\ell:M\otimes X\to\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_W M)\otimes X)$. It is not the inverse of the displayed $\mu_{M,X}$ in general. Choose a common Engel flag $0=X_0\subset X_1\subset\cdots\subset X_t=X$ for the nilpotent $\mathfrak m$ action, so $\mathfrak m X_j\subset X_{j-1}$; a negative-graded Lie algebra acts nilpotently on a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module. The matrix-coefficient construction of $\ell$ preserves this flag and has diagonal $1_\chi\otimes m\otimes x_j$: on each flag quotient the $\mathfrak m$ action is trivial, and the inverse cofree evaluation is precisely the unit $m\mapsto1_\chi\otimes m$. Every correction term involves a strictly flag-lowering matrix coefficient. PBW represents these finitely supported lifts by elements of $U(\mathfrak p)$ acting on $M$; no completion of $M$ is used. The displayed map applies $\eta^{-1}$ of this representative to $M$ and leaves the $X$ component in its flag position. Thus $A=\mu_{M,X}\ell$ preserves $M\otimes X_j$ and is the identity on its successive quotients. Write $A=1+N$; then $N^t=0$, although its off-diagonal entries can be arbitrary operators on $M$. Hence $A^{-1}=\sum_{r=0}^{t-1}(-N)^r$, and $\mu_{M,X}$ is a vector-space isomorphism. This argument distinguishes cofree constant evaluation from the extension-dependent displayed map. [F1, F4, step 1.3, construct, algebra]

2.2 Associativity. The associativity isomorphisms of the transported functor are obtained by inserting the canonical associativity isomorphisms of the tensor product of $\mathfrak g$-modules into the definition of $\circledast$ and applying the inverse equivalence; they are compatible by the naturality of the unit and counit of the adjunction and by the coherence of the tensor associativity in $\mathcal C(\lambda)$. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 **Balancing and $W$-linearity.** PBW gives unique representatives $\eta(u)1_\chi$, $u\in U(\mathfrak p)$, in $Q_\chi$. Define $\psi_M(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)=um$. Since the right action of $w\in W\subset U(\mathfrak p)$ sends this representative to $\eta(uw)1_\chi$, the formula is right-$W$-balanced: $(uw)m=u(wm)$. Moreover $\psi_M(\eta(v)q\otimes m)=v\psi_M(q\otimes m)$ for $v\in U(\mathfrak p)$. The shift $\eta$ adds a Lie character on $\mathfrak p$, so on its primitive generators, and hence multiplicatively on $U(\mathfrak p)$, $(\eta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(v)=\Delta\eta(v)$. The $W$ action on the source Whittaker subspace is therefore $\Delta\eta(w)$, while the target restricted $\mathfrak p$-module $M\otimes X$ has action $\Delta(w)$. Applying $\psi_M\otimes\mathrm{id}$ to the displayed coproduct identity proves $\mu_{M,X}(wz)=w\mu_{M,X}(z)$. Together with step 2.1 this proves the actual stated $W$-module isomorphism. No equality with cofree evaluation or citation-only character-equation argument is used. [F2, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Independence of the order. For $X=V^{\otimes d}$ the isomorphism $\mu_d$ is the composite of the single-step maps $\mu_{\bullet,V}$; two different parenthesizations differ by the associativity isomorphisms of step 2.2, and both are restrictions of the balanced evaluation maps of step 3.1, applied with the same iterated coproduct on $U(\mathfrak p)$; coassociativity and the displayed shift identity make these maps equal. Therefore the resulting isomorphism $\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$ is independent of the composed associativity isomorphisms. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The source's convention is that $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ carries the actual displacement index $r=\mathrm{col}(a)-\mathrm{col}(b)$; coefficients at or below the prefix shift vanish and coefficient $0$ is $\delta_{i,j}$. This is the convention used by the explicit matrices in step 2.1.

- The equivalence is exact but its left adjoint in the Schur-functor constructions later on this page is not the naive tensor functor; those constructions use the projective generator $T$ of a single block, treated later.

items.title: The loop filtration on the type-A finite W-algebra has associated graded U(g^e)
items.statement:
Equip $W(\lambda)$ with the loop (good) filtration
$$F_rW(\lambda)=W(\lambda)\cap\bigoplus_{s\le r}U(\mathfrak p)_s$$
induced by the pyramid grading $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$ of
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], and
likewise for the shifted Yangian of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
Then the associated graded algebra $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)$ is
canonically isomorphic to the enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, viewed as
a graded algebra via the restriction of the pyramid grading, and the
isomorphism sends the leading symbol of the generator $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ to
$(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, where the $e_{i,j;r}$ are the centralizer basis of the
pyramid. In particular $W(\lambda)$ is a filtered deformation of
$U(\mathfrak g^e)$, the loop filtration is separated, and the ordered
monomials in the generators $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$, form a basis of
$W(\lambda)$.

This filtration is not the Kazhdan filtration: the Kazhdan filtration has
associated graded the commutative Slodowy-slice algebra $\mathbb C[S]$, while
here $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g^e)$ is noncommutative in
general.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The pyramid $\lambda$, the finite W-algebra $W(\lambda)$ with its generators $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ and loop filtration, and the centralizer basis $e_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.

[F1] The ordered monomials in the finite $T$-modes $s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}$ form a PBW basis of $W(\lambda)$, and the loop degree of $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ is $r$ ([[thm-ordered-monomial-pbw-basis-for-the-shifted-yangian]], [[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]).

[F2] The leading symbol of $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ in the loop filtration is $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$; the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ with $(i,j,r)\in K$ form a basis of the centralizer $\mathfrak g^e$ and satisfy the matrix-unit commutation relations of $\mathfrak g$ ([[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]], [[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]]).

[F3] Ordered monomials in a basis of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra form a PBW basis of its enveloping algebra ([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]); the associated graded of a filtered algebra is computed from the leading symbols of a filtered basis ([[def-associated-graded-algebra-of-a-filtered-algebra]]).

[F4] The Kazhdan filtration of the Gan-Ginzburg construction has associated graded the commutative coordinate ring of the Slodowy slice, not the enveloping algebra of $\mathfrak g^e$ ([[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]).





## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The PBW basis and leading-symbol data of [F1]-[F2].

1.1 **Actual ambient leading term.** Give a matrix unit $e_{a,b}\in\mathfrak p$ its good degree $\operatorname{col}(b)-\operatorname{col}(a)$. In the explicit signed path formula a term of canonical degree $r+1$ with $k$ matrix-unit factors has good degree at most $r+1-k$; a diagonal scalar replacement only lowers that degree. Therefore only single-factor terms contribute in good degree $r$. Those terms sum to $(-1)^r\sum e_{a,b}$ over $\operatorname{row}(a)=i$, $\operatorname{row}(b)=j$, $\operatorname{col}(b)-\operatorname{col}(a)=r$, namely $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$. Products introduced by Gauss factorization or its inverse have at least two factors and have smaller good degree. Thus the leading homogeneous component of $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ in the actual graded algebra $U(\mathfrak p)$ is exactly $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$. This proves the leading-symbol claim using the path degrees rather than a claim that Gauss inversion alone supplies its sign. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 **Independence in the ambient enveloping algebra.** The elements $e_{i,j;r}$ form a homogeneous basis of the actual Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak g^e\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Extend that finite basis to a homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak p$, with an order extending the prescribed order of the centralizer basis. Enveloping PBW implies that the ordered monomials in the $e_{i,j;r}$ are linearly independent in $U(\mathfrak p)$, and that the natural homomorphism $U(\mathfrak g^e)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ is injective. Their products and brackets are the actual ambient products and brackets, including all boundary terms of the centralizer strings. No projection of a current bracket with an arbitrary out-of-range convention is needed. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Strictness of the loop basis.** The finite $T$ monomials form a vector-space basis of $W(\lambda)$ by [F1]. For a monomial with total loop degree $d$, step 1.1 says that its degree-$d$ homogeneous component in $U(\mathfrak p)$ is, up to the product of its displayed signs, the corresponding PBW monomial in $U(\mathfrak g^e)$. In any nonzero finite linear combination of $T$ monomials, take the largest total loop degree $d$. The degree-$d$ homogeneous component is nonzero by step 1.2, even when degree-zero generators occur. Thus that combination belongs to $\bigoplus_{s\le d}U(\mathfrak p)_s$ and not to $\bigoplus_{s<d}U(\mathfrak p)_s$. Consequently the intersection filtration in the Statement is exactly the span of $T$ monomials of total loop degree at most $d$, and their degree-$d$ symbols form a basis of its associated graded. This verifies symbol independence directly, rather than inferring it from independence of filtered elements. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **The graded algebra isomorphism.** For any subalgebra of a nonnegatively graded algebra with its intersection filtration, taking highest homogeneous components embeds its associated graded into that graded algebra: if a representative's component of degree $d$ is zero it already lies in filtration $d-1$, and multiplication agrees with multiplication of homogeneous components. Apply this to $W(\lambda)\subseteq U(\mathfrak p)$. Step 2.1 identifies its image with the span of the ordered monomials in $\mathfrak g^e$, which is precisely the embedded algebra $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ from step 1.2. Hence $\operatorname{gr}^{\mathrm{loop}}W(\lambda)\cong U(\mathfrak g^e)$, and the identification sends the symbol of $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ to $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$ as asserted. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra, construct]

4.1 **Filtration and the second graded algebra.** Each generator has finite nonnegative good degree, and each element is a finite sum of $T$ monomials, so the loop filtration is exhaustive and bounded below with $F_{-1}=0$. The actual homogeneous decomposition in $U(\mathfrak p)$ and step 2.1 give separatedness. The finite basis is already established in [F1], and step 3.1 establishes its filtered deformation property. Independently, the Kazhdan filtration uses positive weights $\operatorname{col}(b)-\operatorname{col}(a)+1$ on $\mathfrak p$ and has associated graded $\mathbb C[S]$ by [F4]; in the doubled convention its weights are twice these. That graded algebra is commutative, whereas $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ is noncommutative whenever $\mathfrak g^e$ is nonabelian. These are the two claimed filtrations and their respective graded algebras. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The index shift is part of the statement: the generator with loop degree $r$ is $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$, and its symbol is $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$. The coefficient index of the source series is $r+1$, and no additional rescaling is applied.

- The affine-Yangian proof notes expand the coefficient bookkeeping of steps 1.1-1.2 (Gauss inversion signs and the finite range); the finite-W matrix proof contains the tensor-model check of the same symbol assignment.

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra
items.statement:
Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The degenerate affine Hecke algebra $H_d$, a multiset $\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_l)$ of arbitrary complex numbers with $l\ge1$, and its quotient $A=H_d/(f(x_1))$, where $f(t)=\prod_j(t-a_j)$ and the ideal is two-sided. Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the Skryabin/tensor realization used in PBW independence.

[F1] The affine ordered monomials form a basis, $x_i$ commute, and the cross relations are $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$ and $s_ix_i=x_{i+1}s_i-1$. Its generator-fixing anti-involution exists ([[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]).

[F2] The pyramid construction provides $\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak m,e,\chi$ and the automorphism $\eta(E_{ab})=E_{ab}+\delta_{ab}(n-\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h)$. The Whittaker bimodule is $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ with right $W$-action by $\eta$. PBW identifies it as a vector space with $U(\mathfrak p)$ ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], [[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]], [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F3] For any $\mathfrak p$-module $M$ and finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the tensor-isomorphism of [[thm-skryabins-equivalence-for-the-type-a-whittaker-pair]] identifies $\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_W M)\otimes X)$ with $M\otimes X$ by $(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes v\mapsto um\otimes v$. These identifications are natural and compatible with tensor associativity. No cyclotomic quotient is part of this input.

[F4] The Casimir operators on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ satisfy the affine Hecke relations, commute with $\mathfrak g$, and therefore restrict to Whittaker vectors; their naturality transports them through F3 ([[thm-the-casimir-and-place-permutation-operators-satisfy-degenerate-affine-hecke-relations]]).

[F5] Filtered leading symbols multiply in the associated graded ([[def-associated-graded-algebra-of-a-filtered-algebra]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** $A=H_d/(f(x_1))$, the polynomial-degree filtration, and F1–F5; assume AC for F3 and the transported representation.

1.1 Bounded spanning in every variable. For each $r$, put $w_r=s_{r-1}\cdots s_1$ (and $w_1=1$). In the affine algebra the cross relations give $w_rx_1w_r^{-1}=x_r+$ terms of polynomial degree zero. Hence $w_rf(x_1)w_r^{-1}=x_r^l+$ terms of degree at most $l-1$. This element is zero in $A$. Every affine ordered monomial with an exponent at least $l$ can therefore have a factor $x_r^l$ replaced by terms of strictly smaller total polynomial degree; straightening those terms never increases that degree. Induction on total degree, applied to every such replacement, expresses every monomial as a linear combination of $x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$ with $0\le r_i<l$. The same induction proves that $F_mA$ is spanned by bounded monomials of degree at most $m$. [F1, algebra]

1.2 A realization for arbitrary complex roots. For $d\ge1$ choose an integer $n\ge d$ and the rectangular partition $\lambda=(l,\ldots,l)$ with $n$ rows, so every column has height $q_j=n$ and $e$ has $n$ strings of length $l$. On $\mathfrak p$ define the one-dimensional module $\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}$ by $E_{ab}\mapsto\delta_{ab}a_{\mathrm{col}(a)}$. This is a Lie character: it vanishes on the strictly positive nilradical and is $a_j$ times the trace on the $j$th Levi block. In particular no integrality or coset condition on $a_j$ is needed. Restrict this module to $W$ and use F3 with $X=V^{\otimes d}$. Restrict the affine Hecke operators on $(Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_{\mathbf a})\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ to Whittaker vectors, then transport through F3. This defines an affine Hecke action on $V_{\mathbf a}^{\otimes d}=\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}\otimes V^{\otimes d}$; the $s_i$ are place permutations. The following step computes $x_1$ before asserting any quotient factorization. [F2, F3, F4, construct]

1.3 The transported first operator. Write $Q_c=Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}$ and define $\pi_c:Q_c\to\mathbb C$ by $\pi_c(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes1)=u\cdot1$. It is well defined: the right $W$-relations become multiplication by the restricted character, and PBW gives representatives $\eta(u)1_\chi$. For a tensor basis vector $v_{\mathbf j}$ write its unique Whittaker preimage under F3 as $z=\sum_{\mathbf i}z_{\mathbf i}\otimes v_{\mathbf i}$, with $z_{\mathbf i}\in Q_c$. Then $\pi_c(z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$. If $\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b)$, then $E_{ab}\in\mathfrak p$ and $\pi_c(E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{ab}(a_{\mathrm{col}(a)}+\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h-n)\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$, since $\eta^{-1}(E_{ab})=E_{ab}-\delta_{ab}(n-\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h)$. If $\mathrm{col}(a)>\mathrm{col}(b)$, the Whittaker equation for $E_{ab}$ instead gives $E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i}=\chi(E_{ab})z_{\mathbf i}-\sum_{\mathbf k}z_{\mathbf k}$, where $\mathbf k$ runs over tensors obtained from $\mathbf i$ by replacing an occurrence of $a$ by $b$. Apply $\pi_c\otimes1$ to $\Omega_{01}z=\sum_{a,b,\mathbf i}E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i}\otimes E_{ba}^{(1)}v_{\mathbf i}$. The terms with $\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b)$ give $(a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}+\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(j_1)}q_h-n)v_{\mathbf j}$. The $\chi$ term gives $v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}$, because $\chi(E_{ab})=1$ exactly when $b=L(a)$. In the negative sum, replacing the first occurrence gives $-\sum_{h>\mathrm{col}(j_1)}q_h\,v_{\mathbf j}$; replacing an occurrence in position $k>1$ gives $-v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}$ exactly when $\mathrm{col}(j_k)<\mathrm{col}(j_1)$. Consequently the transported right action is
$$v_{\mathbf j}x_1=v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}+(a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}+q_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}-n)v_{\mathbf j}-\sum_{k>1:\ \mathrm{col}(j_k)<\mathrm{col}(j_1)}v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}.$$
Here a nonexistent left-shift term is zero. In our rectangle $q_j=n$, so the diagonal coefficient is precisely $a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 The cyclotomic relation and the leading symbols. Let $C_k$ be the span of tensors whose first entry has column at most $k$, with $C_0=0$. Step 1.3 gives $C_k(x_1-a_k)\subseteq C_{k-1}$: both the left shift and every exchange strictly lower the first column, while $x_1$ preserves $C_{k-1}$. Thus successively applying $(x_1-a_l),\ldots,(x_1-a_1)$ kills $C_l=V^{\otimes d}$. The factors commute, so $f(x_1)=0$ and the action factors through $A$. Grade $V$ by $\deg v_b=l-\mathrm{col}(b)$ and give its endomorphism algebra the induced filtration. In step 1.3 the left shift has degree one and every other term has total tensor degree zero. Hence $\operatorname{gr}_1x_1=e_1$. The recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ shows by induction that all $x_j$ are filtered of degree one with leading symbol $e_j$, and that $s_j$ have degree zero with symbols the place permutations. [F1, F5, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Independence and the associated graded algebra. The cross relations and the conjugated relations in step 1.1 give a surjection $B=\mathbb C[X_1,\ldots,X_d]/(X_1^l,\ldots,X_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}A$. Its composite with the associated graded tensor representation is $X_j\mapsto e_j$, $w\mapsto$ place permutation. Choose the rightmost box in each of $d$ distinct rows and let $v$ be the tensor of those boxes. For bounded $\mathbf r$ and $w$, the vectors $v e_1^{r_1}\cdots e_d^{r_d}w$ are distinct tensor basis vectors: their row labels identify the permutation, and their columns identify all $r_i$. Therefore this composite is injective. It follows that $B\cong\operatorname{gr}A$. Taking leading symbols of a hypothetical linear relation among bounded monomials, first in its largest total degree and then inductively, proves their independence. Along with step 1.1 this gives the claimed PBW basis, its filtration compatibility, and $\dim A=l^dd!$. The longest strings have length $l$, the number of columns, and there are $n=q_l\ge d$ of them; no column height is used as their length. For $d=0$ the algebra, basis and associated graded are all $\mathbb C$, so the assertions hold directly. [F1, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Integral roots and the pyramid dictionary. For integral roots write $m_i=\#\{j:a_j=i\}$; then $f(x_1)=\prod_i(x_1-i)^{m_i}$, the quotient attached to $\Lambda=\sum_i m_i\Lambda_i$. For arbitrary complex roots the same algebraic definition applies, with integer-chain bookkeeping separately in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$. The rectangle above has $c_j=a_j$ and $q_j=n$, hence $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$; the general pyramid dictionary is the displayed diagonal term of step 1.3. No general complex root is identified with an integer-only fundamental-weight index. [step 1.3, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 Level one and the anti-involution. For $l=1$, $x_1=a_1$ and $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ give $x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ by induction; the basis of step 3.1 identifies the quotient with $\mathbb C[S_d]$. The generator-fixing anti-involution fixes $f(x_1)$ and preserves its two-sided ideal, so descends to $A$. [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

4.3 The graded top pairing. Put $D=d(l-1)$ and $T=x_1^{l-1}\cdots x_d^{l-1}$. Let $\tau_0:B\to\mathbb C$ be the coefficient of $X_1^{l-1}\cdots X_d^{l-1}\cdot1$. For graded monomials $X^{\mathbf r}w,X^{\mathbf s}v$, this coefficient is one exactly when $wv=1$ and $\mathbf r+w(\mathbf s)=(l-1,\ldots,l-1)$, and is zero otherwise. The equivalent reversed condition is $vw=1$ and $\mathbf s+w^{-1}(\mathbf r)=(l-1,\ldots,l-1)$; thus $\tau_0$ is symmetric. Each basis element pairs with its unique complementary element, so the pairing is perfect, including between degrees $m$ and $D-m$. Define $\tau:A\to\mathbb C$ as the coefficient of $T\cdot1$ in the PBW basis. By filtration compatibility $\tau=\tau_0\circ\operatorname{gr}_D$ on $A=F_DA$, and it vanishes on $F_{D-1}A$. Therefore, if $a\in F_mA$ and $b\in F_{D-m}A$, then $\tau(ab)=\tau_0(\operatorname{gr}_m(a)\operatorname{gr}_{D-m}(b))=\tau(ba)$. This establishes cyclicity only under the stated degree bound so far. [F5, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Full generator cyclicity. Since permutations have degree zero, step 4.3 gives $\tau(aw)=\tau(wa)$ for every $a\in A$, $w\in S_d$. To check $\tau(x_i b)=\tau(bx_i)$ for all bounded basis monomials $b$, step 4.3 suffices when $\deg b<D$. The remaining ones are exactly $b=Tw$. The polynomial $T$ is central: it commutes with the $x_j$, and the cross relations directly give $s_j(x_jx_{j+1})=(x_jx_{j+1})s_j$, while $s_j$ commutes with the other variables. Hence $s_jT=Ts_j$. Applying the already proved permutation cyclicity twice gives $\tau(x_iTw)=\tau(wx_iT)=\tau(wTx_i)=\tau(Twx_i)$. This proves cyclicity with every generator on every element; successively moving generators of a word from the beginning to the end proves $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ for all $a,b\in A$. It also covers $l=1$ (where $T=1$ and $D=0$). [F1, step 4.3, algebra]

6.1 Nondegeneracy and block restriction. For $0\ne a\in A$, take its largest filtration degree $m$, so $\operatorname{gr}_m(a)\ne0$. By the perfect graded pairing of step 4.3 choose homogeneous $b_0\in B_{D-m}$ with $\tau_0(\operatorname{gr}_m(a)b_0)\ne0$, and lift it to $b\in F_{D-m}A$. Then $\tau(ab)\ne0$. Thus the pairing has zero left radical, and symmetry gives zero right radical; this proves nondegeneracy without claiming that products of excess total degree have zero trace. If $e$ is a central idempotent and $0\ne a\in eA$, choose $b$ as above; then $\tau(aeb)=\tau(ab)\ne0$, so the restriction to $eA=eAe$ is nondegenerate and symmetric as well. [F5, step 4.3, step 5.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The integer and nonintegral cases are kept separate on purpose: the integral case is the classical cyclotomic quotient of the type-A root system, while the general complex roots are handled through the pyramid realization whose columns are chosen large enough to make the tensor action faithful.

- The trace of steps 4.3, 5.1 and 6.1 is the top PBW coefficient functional; it is the tool that rules out nonzero ideals in the radical in the double centralizer arguments on this page.

items.title: The deformed tensor space for the type-A finite W-algebra
items.statement:
Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.
items.strategy: Assume AC for the actual Skryabin and Vust suppliers. The column-trace Lie character $\kappa_c(X)=\sum_b c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb})$ defines the total origin twist once. Use the actual balanced $\mu$ and ambient trace-form Casimir; evaluation on its Whittaker preimages separates nonnegative-column terms, negative character terms, first-position replacements and cross-position replacements, giving exactly the displayed raw $x_1$. Thus affine relations and commutation are transported with $W$, not with all of $\mathfrak p$. First-column filtration gives the full cyclotomic polynomial, and the total tensor grading gives its exact minimal degree, including repeated roots. Restrict the column character to the fixed basis: $\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{ij}\delta_{r0}\sum_{b\le p_i}c_b$. The graded automorphism $\tau_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ preserves $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, and the full fixed-chart graded representation is $\operatorname{gr}\Phi_{d,c}=\varphi_{d,0}\tau_c\zeta$, including its surviving degree-zero scalar. Keep the actual $T=FDE$ coefficient index, $T^{(r+1)}$ loop degree $r$ and sign $(-1)^r$. The right symbols are individual $e$ operators and places. Since $\tau_c$ is a unital automorphism, the exact character-twisted representation has the same unital graded image and commutant as untwisted Vust. Prove the two full filtered centralizer identities by the chains $A^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)\subseteq Z(D^0)=A^0$ and its reverse counterpart, then finite descending subtraction. Handle $d=0$ with the nontrivial character on the scalar module and the empty pyramid by its zero/scalar identities. Rank-one $c_1=1,d=1$ yields fixed generator $E_{11}=2$, not untwisted $1$; the $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ example gives $[E_{11}-E_{22},x_1]=2E_{12}\ne0$. All origins, shapes and degrees are retained; no stable range or admissibility is used. Mathematical acceptance and actual-supplier/consumer closure remain with the original reviewer.
