items.title: The parabolic highest-weight truncation factors through the cyclotomic quotient
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] only for the imported
Skryabin equivalence identifying the raw Whittaker bimodule and its affine
action. The finite raw-matrix polynomial and minimal-polynomial calculations
and the ordinary $P_c\otimes V$ column-flag calculation are choice-free.

Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a nonempty pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l>0$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be arbitrary complex origins,
and put $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for $1\le j\le l$. For $d\ge1$ consider the raw
tensor operator $x_1$ on the truncated tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]] (whose underlying
space is $V^{\otimes d}$ and whose $x_1$ is the operator displayed there).
Then the minimal polynomial of $x_1$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is exactly
$$\prod_{j=1}^l(x-a_j),$$
including repeated roots with their multiplicities. Consequently the action of
$H_d$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ factors through the cyclotomic quotient
$H_d(\mathbf a)$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. The same
polynomial annihilates the action of the ordinary Casimir operator on
$P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, where $P_c$ is the ground induced module with its
genuine column filtration.

The statement does not assert that every unrelated standard object $N(A)$, or
every parabolic category-$\mathcal O$ object, carries that same tensor action.
For $d=0$ there is no operator $x_1$. The integral-root weight $\Lambda$ and
the arbitrary-root coset bookkeeping are the separate conventions of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].
items.strategy: Define the full raw operator locally with the sum over every later tensor position $k=2,\ldots,d$, using the same physical box labels and arbitrary origins. Assume AC only for the actual Skryabin equivalence used to establish this raw affine action: evaluate its balanced tensor map on actual Whittaker preimages and separate the diagonal, negative character, first-position and later-position terms to recover the raw display. This model is $Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_c$, not the ordinary ground module. The first-column flag $C_b$ satisfies $C_b(x_1-a_b)\subseteq C_{b-1}$, so every column factor, including repeated roots, annihilates in succession. With total grading $\deg v_j=l-\operatorname{col}(j)$, the left shift has degree one and each cross-position exchange degree zero; hence $\operatorname{gr}_1x_1=e^{(1)}$, and nonvanishing powers below $l$ prove exact minimal degree. The affine action therefore factors through the cyclotomic quotient. Separately define the ordinary ground module $P_c=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}\mathbb C_\mu$, with $\mu_b=c_b+\sum_{h\le b}q_h-n$. PBW right-freeness and the coproduct tensor identity induce the natural column flag on $P_c\otimes V$, not on $P_c$ itself. On a ground tensor $m_0\otimes v_j$, $\Omega=\sum E_{ab}\otimes E_{ba}$ contributes $\mu_b$ from the diagonal, zero from non-diagonal parabolic terms, and subtracts one for each earlier-column box after rewriting the lower-block term through the tensor identity. The other term lands in the earlier flag piece. Thus the quotient scalar is $\mu_b-\sum_{h<b}q_h=c_b+q_b-n=a_b$. Ambient $\mathfrak g$-linearity extends this to the entire quotient and preserves the flag, proving the same annihilating polynomial on $P_c\otimes V$. Tensoring the remaining factors proves the ordinary $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ claim. Handle $d=0$ without a nonexistent $x_1$. Preserve arbitrary complex origins, every nonempty shape and repeated-root multiplicities. No ordinary-to-plain-Skryabin identification, FDE reindexing or integral-category identification is used.

items.title: Separated integral cosets give typed parabolic category equivalences
items.statement:
Assume AC. Work in genuine type-$A$ parabolic category $\mathcal O$ for
$\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its fixed Borel. Its column Levi has ordered
blocks of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. All entries in column $j$ lie in
$c_j+\mathbb Z$, where the original admissibility condition is
$c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z\Rightarrow c_j=c_k$. Use the source highest-weight
convention $\eta_i=a_i+i-1$ and half-sum
$\rho_i=(N+1-2i)/2$, with the column reading prescribed by the source Borel.
For each occurring entry coset $\kappa$ retain its columns in their original
order. Fix an order on the finite set of cosets; no order on $\mathbb C$ is used.

Subject to the local HC tensor-projective comparison stated in [F1], stable
sorting of the coordinates by $\kappa$ gives an exact, complex-linear
equivalence of the genuine parabolic categories, carrying each ordinary
Verma label by the dot permutation and carrying the corresponding generalized
standard, simple head and projective cover. On each linkage block, the sorted
category is equivalent to the product of the corresponding parabolic blocks
for $\mathfrak{gl}_{N_\kappa}$, where
$N_\kappa=\sum_{j\in\kappa}q_j$. Product means the abelian category generated
by finite presentations of outer tensor products, equivalently modules over
the tensor product of the finite block endomorphism algebras.

For the original pyramid with $n$ rows put $n_\kappa=\max_{j\in\kappa}q_j$.
The component integral entry dictionary is exactly
$$a_i^{\mathrm{int}}=a_i-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa,\qquad m_j=q_j-n_\kappa,\qquad \inf I_\kappa=1-n_\kappa.$$
Thus $m_j+1-\inf I_\kappa=q_j$, with the original nonincreasing retained
heights and charges. For the admitted-ground subcategories, where each original entry has a
nonnegative integral difference from its own ground entry, this dictionary
lands in the bounded-below admitted integral component models of [F4]. For
other genuine parabolic blocks it records the integral weight/coset
dictionary and the trace shift, without asserting membership in that fixed
admitted cut. If the component follows $B_\kappa$ sorted coordinates, its
Levi highest weight and the integral highest weight differ by the scalar
trace-character shift
$$\delta_\kappa=B_\kappa+c_\kappa-n+n_\kappa.$$
This shift is a Lie algebra character and requires no integrality of
$c_\kappa$. Singular repeated-entry linkage blocks are included. The original
complex origins, component entry multisets and their scalar centres remain
recorded; different complex cosets are not merged into one integral block.

Sorting commutes coherently with finite tensoring and its invariant Casimir
and permutation maps. The separated product decomposition is blockwise and
does not assert that unrestricted tensoring is componentwise. The proof gives
its actual filtration and block-projection comparison. Choices of sorting
word with the same stable permutation yield the natural comparison fixed on
the chosen reference highest vector and its tensor-projective presentations.

Fixed admitted integral cut used only under admitted-ground hypothesis.

items.title: The Whittaker functor from the relevant parabolic category-O summand
items.statement:
Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines finite tensoring, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.
items.strategy:
**Given:** The pyramid $\lambda$, admissible origins $c$, the categories $\mathcal O_c^d$ and the Whittaker data; assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the stated imported constructions and Baer/vector-space splittings.

[F1] The parabolic and genuine-category-O interfaces: $P_c$ is the ground simple projective-injective, the standard objects $N(A)$ and simple objects $L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ are labelled by column-strict tableaux, and the category is a highest-weight category with enough projectives ([[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]], [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]], [[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]).

[F2] The finite W-algebra, its Whittaker category and Skryabin's equivalence, including the filtration $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-$ and the tensor identification $M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X)$ on restricted $\mathfrak p$-modules ([[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]], [[thm-skryabins-equivalence-for-the-type-a-whittaker-pair]], [[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]).

[F3] The truncated tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a filtered $(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule with the explicit generators, and the tensor compatibility preserves the generators $x_j,s_i$ ([[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]).

[F4] The typed nonintegral category comparison and admitted-ground coset dictionaries are supplied by [[lem-nonintegral-harish-chandra-tensor-projective-comparison]] and [[lem-separated-integral-cosets-give-typed-parabolic-category-equivalences]]. Standard/Casimir/Fock interfaces: the highest-weight truncation, the Specht-to-permutation dominance comparison, the Weyl character formula computation, BGG reciprocity and the Fock-basis dictionaries on the source side ([[thm-schur-weyl-decomposition-with-length-cutoff]], [[thm-specht-to-permutation-homomorphism-dominance]], [[thm-weyl-character-formula]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]], [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]], [[thm-duflo-joseph-g-finite-endomorphisms-of-verma-modules]], [[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]], [[prop-base-change-freeness-and-specialization-in-the-deformed-family]], [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]).

[F5] Noetherianity, Baer injectivity, complete reducibility and Hilbert basis inputs used to make the functorial constructions finite and exact ([[thm-hilbert-basis-theorem]], [[thm-baer-criterion-for-injective-modules]], [[thm-weyls-complete-reducibility-theorem]], [[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** Assume AC. Use $U=U(\mathfrak m)$ and $I=I_\chi$. The source standards are $N(A)$, source simples $L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ (abbreviated $L_O(A)$ in the computations), and output simples $L_W(A)$. The finite tensor/Hopf comparisons use the actual Skryabin displayed map, not cofree constant evaluation.

1.1 Let U=U(m), I=I_chi. Replace x by y=x−chi(x). These shifted generators have the original brackets, because chi vanishes on brackets. Choose a basis adapted to the lower-central filtration, with weight w_i the largest lower-central index containing its basis vector. PBW reordering and the commutator formula show that I^n is spanned by ordered monomials of total lower-central weight≥n: one inclusion follows from reordering n factors, while the reverse follows because each basis vector of weight w lies in I^w, being a linear combination of iterated brackets of length w. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.2 The Rees algebra R=⊕_(n≥0) I^n t^n is generated by y_i t^r, 0≤r≤w_i. Their span is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra: a nonzero bracket component y_k has w_k≥w_i+w_j, so r+s≤w_k. PBW gives its enveloping algebra a polynomial associated graded. For any left ideal, Hilbert basis gives finitely many generators of its homogeneous leading ideal; lift them and subtract matching highest-degree terms until the nonnegative degree decreases to zero. The lifts generate the original ideal. Thus the enveloping algebra is left noetherian, and its surjection onto R makes R left noetherian. For a left ideal J⊂U, ⊕(J∩I^n)t^n is a graded left ideal of R and has finitely many homogeneous generators. For fixed k, choosing n greater than k plus their largest degrees gives J∩I^n⊂I^k J. This is the precise Artin–Rees consequence needed here. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.3 Set E_chi=∪_(n≥0)(U/I^n)^*, with left action (x f)(r)=f(r x). To prove injectivity, take a U-linear map phi:J→E_chi. U is noetherian, so choose finitely many generators of J. A common I^k kills their images and hence all images, since I is two-sided. The scalar functional lambda(j)=phi(j)(1) kills I^k J. Choose n with J∩I^n⊂I^k J, extend lambda from J/(J∩I^n) to U/I^n, and call the extension a∈E_chi. The map U→E_chi, u↦u a, extends phi, because at r its value on j is a(rj)=phi(rj)(1)=phi(j)(r). Baer's criterion gives injectivity. This supplies the injective-continuous-dual assertion cited without proof in BK Lemma8.20. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.4 For a U(m)-finitely generated g-module X, evaluation at1 identifies Hom_m(X,E_chi) with the scalar functionals lambda:X→C that kill I^n X for some n. Indeed, reconstruct the map by F_lambda(v)(r)=lambda(rv); finitely many generators give a common n. The right U(g)-action is (lambda·u)(v)=lambda(uv). On E-valued maps its formula is therefore [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.5 (F·u)(v)(r)=lambda(u r v), [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.6 not the generally non-m-linear expression F(uv)(r)=lambda(r u v). This distinguishes the compressed scalar-functional notation in the source from a literal E-valued composition. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.7 The right action preserves continuity. For a fixed u∈U(g), the finite PBW subspace generated by all iterated ad m on u is finite-dimensional and its negative-column action is nilpotent; sufficiently long products of ad m vanish. Moving u past a product of sufficiently many shifted m generators therefore leaves at least n of them on the left. Equivalently u I^(n+C)⊂I^n U(g) for some C=C(u). Thus lambda u kills I^(n+C)X. On this continuous-dual module the right shifted m-action is locally nilpotent. Injectivity of E_chi makes Hom_m(−,E_chi) exact, and right Skryabin makes its Whittaker vectors exact. These Whittaker vectors are precisely Hom_m(X,C_chi). Dualizing this finite-dimensional vector space gives an exact covariant functor. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.8 The restricted dual uses the row-sum torus a=span{Σ_(row(j)=r)E_jj}, not the full Cartan and not the column-origin vector c. Every e-adjacent pair lies in one row, so chi has a-weight0. If X is generated over U(m) by finitely many a-weight spaces, an m-linear functional into C_chi vanishes outside those finitely many weights: lambda(uv)=chi(u)lambda(v), and chi(u)=0 in every nonzero a-weight. Thus the restricted-dual definition agrees with the entire finite-dimensional Hom space. Generalized parabolic Vermas are U(m)-free on a finite-dimensional Levi module by PBW; their finite projective flags/presentations from the repaired parabolic highest-weight supplier make every genuine parabolic O object finitely generated over U(m). This establishes exactness on precisely that category. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.9 For X=U(g)⊗_(U(p))X_0, the Hom space is canonically X_0^*. The finite-W action on its covariant dual uses the right-model head twist eta_head(E_jj)=E_jj+n−Σ_(k≤col(j))q_k. The left-model twist is eta_tail(E_jj)=E_jj+n−Σ_(k≥col(j))q_k. Their numerical difference is −tr_m(ad E_jj), since the trace counts earlier minus later column heights. This numerical identity does not by itself prove equality of the two W models. The actual identification of the left/right W models and compatibility on all shifted-Yangian generators is the explicit matrix-generator check in the companion finite-W matrix note; the vector-space duality alone does not supply it. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.10 Reflect the pyramid and transpose matrix units with its column-renumbering permutation. This is an anti-isomorphism of U(g). Reversing each path preserves its degree, sign and cut inequalities and sends P_ij;x to P'_ji;x term by term. The shift matrix is transposed. The preceding reflected generator theorem therefore identifies the reflected W and the transpose images of the original generators. Applying this anti-isomorphism to its left reduction condition turns the left ideal into the right ideal and its tail shift into the original head shift. Consequently the SAME original W subalgebra equals {u:[eta_head(u),m]⊂I_chi U(g)}. Numerically eta_head−eta_tail=−tr_m ad on each diagonal matrix; this equality is explained by the column counts but is not used as a substitute for the path-transpose proof. [F2, F3, construct, algebra]

1.11 Fix an admissible origin: c_j−c_k integral implies c_j=c_k. The original arbitrary-origin deformed tensor algebra remains separate and unrestricted. In a column of height q whose global row numbers are n−q+1,…,n, write its strict entries a_1,…,a_q. The genuine head-model V action makes its finite-Levi highest weight nu_s=a_s+n−q+s−1. This follows directly from the global highest weight lambda_i=a_i+i−1 and eta_head diagonal shift n−q_1−…−q_col: the column-reading position i=q_before+(global_row−n+q) gives lambda_i+eta_head=a_i+global_row−1. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.12 Finite-Levi Weyl gives, on row variables z_(n−q+1),…,z_n, [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.13 ch L(nu)=det(z_r^(nu_s+q−s))/det(z_r^(q−s)) =(Π_(r=n−q+1)^n z_r^(n−1)) det(z_r^(a_s))/det(z_r^(q−s)). [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.14 The numerator exponent is exactly a_s+n−1; the column height and reading offset cancel. The prefactor and denominator are independent of the entries. Products over columns therefore identify the row-torus character of V(N(A)) with a fixed factor times products of nested bottom-row flag minors, evaluated at y_(r,a)=z_r^a. For the ground column a_s=c+1−(n−q+s), the determinant cancels the Vandermonde and gives precisely Π z_r^c, verifying the origin normalization. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.15 All exponential expressions lie in the group algebra of the finite subgroup generated by their occurring complex weights and the integral row weights. That subgroup is finitely generated and torsion free, hence free abelian; its group algebra is a Laurent polynomial domain. The nonzero Vandermonde may therefore be cancelled. A zero character of an actual nonzero finite-dimensional module is impossible: its coefficients are nonnegative weight dimensions, and evaluation of the group algebra at1 is its positive dimension. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.16 Fix a finite entry alphabet U, and introduce independent variables y_(r,a), with row space C^n and entry space U. Antisymmetrizing each column of a tensor gives its bottom-row minor, and multiplying gives a GL(U)-linear map from the column-wedge tensor F to Sym(C^n⊗U). Each minor is killed by the lower-row raising operators: replacing a present row by a later row duplicates a row inside its bottom-row set. The product has row weight (p_1,…,p_n). [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.17 Classical Cauchy decomposition follows from the actual published Schur–Weyl decomposition: identify the degree-N symmetric power with diagonal S_N invariants of (C^n)^tensor N⊗U^tensor N, then use the two Specht decompositions. The needed self-duality is complex linear: polytabloids have real coefficients, so their span is conjugation-stable; the bilinear tabloid form B(v,w)=sum v_T w_T is invariant and B(v,conjugate(v)) is the positive Hermitian norm. It is therefore nondegenerate on the Specht span. Schur's lemma with this explicit bilinear duality leaves one multiplicity space for each matching partition. The lower-row highest-weight line at (p_1,…,p_n) selects the partition (p_n,…,p_1), so the entire flag-minor image lies in the irreducible entry module of highest weight Lambda=Σ_j omega_(q_j). The ground product of minors is a nonzero polynomial. Hence the image is exactly this irreducible module. Actual16 proves that this constituent occurs once in F; therefore this nonzero normalized map has exactly the kernel of actual16's highest-component projection pi. No quantum flag algebra or quantum Peter–Weyl theorem is imported. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.18 For different complex cosets, first apply the companion typed category equivalence and use one independent set of variables for each coset. The same Cauchy proof applies to each coset's columns, with their retained sorted heights. Multiplication across the disjoint variable sets is injective on the tensor product. Thus the kernel is the sum of the component projection kernels, exactly the off-standard lower-basis kernel of the product of actual16 models. The shift a↦a−c_kappa+n−n_kappa and inf I_kappa=1−n_kappa is explicit in that companion proof. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.19 V is exact on the genuine parabolic category and sends N(A) to its finite-Levi standard V(A). Actual16 identifies [L_O(A)] with its source lower/dual-canonical vector L_A at parameter1. Its projection pi L_A is zero exactly off Std. The preceding flag-minor factorization consequently gives zero row-torus character of V(L_O(A)) for every off-standard A. Positivity of actual module characters makes V(L_O(A))=0. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.20 The kernel of the Grothendieck map of V is stable under every residue e/f operator, because the actual tensor identity and Casimir/flip compatibility give V e=e V and V f=f Wh. Thus after quotienting by the already-known off-standard kernel, any additional kernel would be a submodule of actual16's irreducible highest component (or the irreducible tensor product for the direct sum of coset root algebras). The ground class survives: its V image is the one-dimensional C_c by the induced-module computation. Hence no additional kernel exists. Every Std simple therefore has a nonzero V image. This argument does not presume that image simple, does not rely on injectivity of the exponential evaluation on the entire abstract polynomial module, and does not require a classification of all finite-dimensional W simples. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.21 Take finite alphabets containing the relevant finite labels and tensor words, with the proved boundary block projections; actual16 gives compatibility under enlarging the cuts. The argument applies on each cut and hence to every object in the selected finite degree/category. All comparisons use integer order within a coset, not an order on C. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.22 The ground P_c is a simple projective-injective by the actual16 integral model and the typed coset product. Tensor biadjunction makes T=P_c⊗V^tensor d projective-injective. Its indecomposable summands are precisely the Std prinjectives, with possible multiplicities; it is a detecting object, not a generator of the whole parabolic category. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.23 Hd acts on T by the universal tensor Casimir. At the first tensor step, the finite p flag of V has one standard section for each column. On its jth section, the Casimir identity Omega=(C_total−C_source−C_V)/2 gives eigenvalue c_j+q_j−n. The column-order flag therefore makes Π_j(x_1−(c_j+q_j−n)) annihilate T; the remaining factors are untouched at higher degree. Thus the cyclotomic action genuinely exists on T, not merely on its V image M=V_c^tensor d. The explicit V tensor comparison transports this action to M. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.24 The filtered Vust theorem gives End_W(M)^op=B, the cyclotomic tensor image. V maps End_g(T)^op into B, and its image contains B because every Hecke operator came from T. This map is injective: a nonzero endomorphism has nonzero image inside T; that image has a Std socle factor by actual16 prinjectivity, so exact V with its established simple kernel cannot kill it. Thus End_g(T)^op=B. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.25 Choose a full finite projective generator Q of the genuine O summand containing T as an explicit summand and write its algebra as A; the projector onto T is e and B=eAe. The exact Schur functor is e(−). It kills precisely the offStd simples. Its left adjoint Ae⊗_B− is right exact and satisfies e(Ae⊗X)=X. The counit Ae⊗eN→N has kernel and cokernel killed by e. Applying V sends it to an isomorphism. Therefore V factors through e(−), and its factor F on B-mod is naturally M⊗_B− by finite free presentations. This factor is exact: the only failure of exactness after the left adjoint is killed by e and hence by Wh. It is faithful, since every B-simple is eL_O(A) for a Std label and its V image is nonzero; exactness then detects every nonzero image of a morphism. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

1.26 A finite-dimensional right B-module whose tensor functor is exact is projective. Explicitly, take its finite projective cover P→M with kernel K⊂P rad B. Tensor the inclusion K→P with B/rad B; flatness makes K/K rad B inject into P/P rad B, but this map is zero, so Nakayama gives K=0. Faithfulness forces every right indecomposable projective to occur in M: otherwise tensor with the corresponding left simple would vanish. Thus M_B is a progenerator. The first filtered centralizer identity gives Wd=End_B(M). The usual generator presentation/evaluation argument now gives the genuine Morita equivalence Wd-mod≃B-mod. In particular F sends B-simples to Wd-simples, proving the full relevant V simple-image claim without assuming it earlier. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

2.1 Tensor compatibility follows from the continuous-dual evaluation, ordinary finite tensor adjunction and the actual balanced Skryabin map: its coproduct identity carries the Casimir and flips to the deformed tensor model. Thus $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and $V(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})=V_c^{\otimes d}$. The preceding kernel/Morita construction proves $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))=L_W(A)$ for standard labels and zero otherwise; it never asserts that the image of a source standard $N(A)$ is simple. The normalized comparison is determined on the ground and its tensor words, hence on the detecting tensor bimodule and on finite free quotient presentations through the established exact Morita factorization. Its ground normalization removes scalar ambiguity. This proves the stated properties of the genuine Whittaker functor, while keeping it distinct from the Hecke Hom quotient. [F1, F2, F3, F4, choose, construct, algebra] ∎

items.title: The finite W and degenerate cyclotomic Hecke actions satisfy a double centralizer
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let
$W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the
image of the finite W-algebra and let
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$ and every $d$, and their associated graded image
   algebras are the corresponding images of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and of the
   truncated polynomial/permutation algebra.
2. If $q_l\ge d$, then the action of the full cyclotomic algebra
   $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful.
3. If $c$ is admissible (that is, $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$),
   then the tensor module is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence
   between $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.

Mutual centralizers alone do not imply Morita for arbitrary $c$: the explicit
example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$ on the companion page has a
nonprojective tensor module.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The pyramid $\lambda$, an origin $c$, the truncated tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$, and the image algebras $W_d$, $B_d$.

[F1] In the fixed loop chart, the associated graded left representation is the character-twisted Vust representation $X\mapsto\sum_tX^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}$. Its unital image is exactly the untwisted Vust image, because it is obtained by the automorphism $X\mapsto X+\kappa_c(X)1$ of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$. The right graded image is the ordinary truncated polynomial/permutation image. These image algebras are mutual centralizers for every Jordan type and every degree, including scalar degree zero and the empty-pyramid zero tensor case ([[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]], [[thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type-a-nilpotent-centralizer]]).

[F2] $W(\lambda)$ has a separated loop filtration with associated graded $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, and the cyclotomic quotient has the bounded monomial basis $x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$ with $0\le r_i<l$; both filtrations are compatible with the bimodule structure ([[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]], [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]).

[F3] Skryabin's equivalence and the Whittaker functor give the representation-theoretic model in which the tensor module is a module over the relevant Hecke image; the Morita statement under admissibility is proved through the exact quotient and progenerator argument ([[thm-skryabins-equivalence-for-the-type-a-whittaker-pair]], [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]]).

[F4] The stable injectivity criterion: if $e$ has at least $d$ strings of maximum length $l$, the longest-string vector realizes the regular right module, so the right action is injective ([[thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type-a-nilpotent-centralizer]]).

[F5] The external standard/Casimir interfaces recorded in [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] supply the admissible character/quotient computations.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The filtered bimodule $V_c^{\otimes d}$, its actual character-twisted graded representation and its unchanged unital Vust image algebras.

1.1 The graded unital images. Write $E=V^{\otimes d}$, $C=W_d$, and $D$ for the right Hecke image viewed as an algebra of operators on $E$. The supplied actual tensor model in F1 gives commuting filtered operator algebras, with the graded symbols containing the unital images $A^0$ of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and $D^0$ of the truncated polynomial/permutation algebra. The character automorphism in F1 gives exactly the same $A^0$ as the untwisted representation; no equality of the fixed-chart twisted and untwisted modules is inferred. Since $A^0,D^0$ are mutual centralizers, taking leading homogeneous terms of commuting operators gives $A^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)\subseteq Z(D^0)=A^0$, where $Z$ is the commutant in $\operatorname{End}(E)$. Interchanging $C,D$ gives $D^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}D\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(C)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}C)\subseteq Z(A^0)=D^0$. Thus every inclusion is equality, establishing strict equality of both graded images as well as their commutants. [F1, F2, construct, algebra]

2.1 The filtered centralizers. For an operator in $Z(D)$, equality of the induced graded spaces in step 1.1 supplies a member of $C$ with the same leading symbol. Subtracting lowers its integer filtration degree. The finite grading of $E$ bounds the induced endomorphism filtration below, so this terminates, proving $Z(D)=C$. The same procedure proves $Z(C)=D$. Returning to the right-action opposite convention gives both mutual-centralizer identities and the stated associated graded image algebras. At degree zero both images are scalar, while for an empty pyramid and positive degree $E=0$ and both are zero; these are already covered by the actual tensor model of F1. This proves clause (1) for every origin, without a Morita assumption. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Stable injectivity. If $q_l\ge d$, then $e$ has at least $d$ strings of maximum length $l$, so by [F4] the right action is injective on the associated graded; a nonzero element of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ has nonzero leading symbol and therefore nonzero image, so the full cyclotomic action is faithful. [F4, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 Morita under admissibility. Assume $c$ admissible. By [F3] and [F5] the tensor module is a right $B_d$-progenerator on the relevant block: the exact Whittaker quotient and the Morita argument identify $\operatorname{Hom}_W(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ with an equivalence, and the first centralizer identity of step 2.1 identifies $W_d$ with the endomorphism algebra of the progenerator. This proves the Morita statement; the same argument does not apply to nonadmissible origins. [F3, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The nonadmissible boundary. For $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$, the explicit finite matrix computed from the tensor action shows that the tensor module is not projective over $B_d$, so the progenerator hypothesis fails; the mutual centralizers of step 2.1 still hold. This is the companion-page example separating the two assertions. [step 2.1, given] ∎

items.title: The Whittaker functor is exact and fully faithful on the required projectives
items.statement: For admissible c the genuine Whittaker functor is exact on O_c^d, and γ:Hom_g(T,−)→Hom_W(V_c^tensor d,V(−)) is a natural isomorphism. Both V and the Hecke quotient are fully faithful on ALL projective objects; the quotient is also fully faithful on tiltings. T is a self-dual prinjective detecting object containing all Std-labelled projective-injective covers, not a generator of the entire O summand. V(T) is a projective generator of W_d-mod and V preserves projectivity on add(T). It need not send every O projective to a W_d-projective. Its composite with the Morita equivalence is the Serre quotient killing exactly offStd simples.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Construct Z_A from finite column symmetric powers, embed it into V^tensor d by symmetrization and PBW induce. Split the last column and append its ground label: maximal physical-prefix inequalities force every possible larger polynomial label to retain that same ground column. Positive-radical invariants of a simple are its top Levi simple, proved using the nondegenerate contravariant form. Adjunction gives a single head; exact top centre sections and Levi BGG give the projective-cover character, so the lifted cover is an isomorphism. Induct over columns, then tensor the remaining finite symmetric powers. Specht-to-permutation dominance gives every projective cover once among these Z_A summands. The quotient T/Z_A has a standard flag, hence Std socle by actual16; its injective hull is in add(T). Thus every projective has a two-term add(T) copresentation. For the corner right adjoint G=Hom_B(eA,−), the unit on T is injective, splits by injectivity, and its torsion complementary summand vanishes by adjunction. Left exact G applied to a copresentation gives unit isomorphisms on every projective, proving full faithfulness. Modules with Std head and targets with Std socle give the same Hom argument, proving tilting faithfulness. Morita and the counit factorization give γ. The rank-one dominant Verma maps to a nonprojective simple over C[x]/x², while add(T) maps to projectives. The complete argument is Whittaker-quotient §§4–6, not the false full-generator inference.

items.statement: For admissible origins, T_α is the central component of the self-dual prinjective detector T=P_c tensor V^tensor d. On the integral model it is sum_(i∈I_α) f_i_d…f_i_1 P_c. Put B_α=End_g(T_α)^op, the corresponding component of the Hecke IMAGE algebra. The exact Schur quotient is π_α=Hom_g(T_α,−); its left adjoint π*_α=T_α tensor_(B_α)− is right exact. It sends B_α-projectives to O-projectives, and π*_α π_α recovers add(T_α), including every Std-labelled prinjective. Neither exactness of π* nor recovery of every O projective is asserted: both fail in the two-equal-charge rank-one example. These components assemble as locally unital sums; all ambient labels, including those killed by π, remain in the O category. The opposite composition/right-action convention is fixed throughout.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Use the actual Whittaker/Hecke factorization and choose a full finite O projective generator with T as a summand. Its idempotent e identifies π with e(−), giving exactness and the Serre quotient directly. Tensor-Hom gives the left adjoint and its right exactness. Free B modules map to copies of T, and projective summands remain projective. The evaluation isomorphism on add(T) proves the recovery clause. In the rank-one block, π(P_dom)=C and π*π(P_dom)=T/xT is the costandard, not P_dom; tensoring (x)→B with the C summand of T_B shows failure of exactness. AC is inherited from projective covers, duality and the locally unital assembly. This is Whittaker-quotient §6.

items.title: Stable range and block idempotent corner for higher-level Schur-Weyl duality
items.statement:
Keep the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c$, and the truncated tensor space
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. The **stable
range** for $\lambda$ is the condition
$$q_l\ge d:$$
at least $d$ Jordan strings have the maximum length $l=p_n$, equivalently the
smallest column has height at least $d$.

The verification below records the structure attached to the stable range and
to its failure. In the stable range the raw $H_d(\mathbf a)$ action is
faithful. For admissible $c$ outside the stable range, the image of the Hecke
action is a central block corner
$$fH_d(\mathbf a)f,$$
where $f$ is the sum of the central blocks supporting the contractible simple
labels: one enlarges the pyramid by adding $r$ full ground rows, keeping the number $l$ of columns fixed, and enlarging every
$q_j$ by $r$ while preserving every root $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$, lets $e$ be the
idempotent selecting the added ground rows, identifies the supported blocks,
and deletes the added rows. The generalized-eigenvalue idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$
are not individually central; $f$ is a sum of entire central blocks, so the
corner is a two-sided algebraic object. For nonadmissible $c$ the genuine
image algebra and the full tensor double centralizer still exist by
[[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]],
but the same central-corner/Morita conclusion is not inferred without
admissibility.
items.strategy:
**Given:** The pyramid $\lambda$, the origins $c$, the truncated tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$, and the Hecke image $B_d\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$.

[F1] The double centralizer and stable injectivity statements are available; the stable range condition is $q_l\ge d$ ([[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]], [[thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type-a-nilpotent-centralizer]]).

[F2] The cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\mathbf a)$ has the bounded monomial basis and finite dimension $l^dd!$; its finite-dimensional modules decompose into generalized weight spaces with idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ summing to $1$ ([[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]).

[F3] Finite-dimensional algebras have projective covers, and the regular module decomposes into projective indecomposables indexed by the simple modules ([[thm-projective-covers-exist-and-are-unique-for-finite-dimensional-algebras]], [[cor-the-regular-module-decomposes-into-projective-indecomposables]]).

[F4] The enlargement construction: adding full ground rows, keeping $l$ fixed, to the pyramid while keeping the roots $a_j$ fixed is the admissible-origin enlargement used by the source, and the resulting tensor modules restrict to the original one on the supported blocks ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]]).

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The stable range condition and the Hecke image $B_d$.

1.1 Faithfulness in the stable range. If $q_l\ge d$, then $e$ has at least $d$ strings of maximum length and the stable injectivity of the Vust theorem makes the right action of the truncated polynomial/permutation algebra faithful on the associated graded; since the $H_d(\mathbf a)$ action has the bounded monomial basis and the filtration is separated, a nonzero element has nonzero leading symbol and hence nonzero image. So the raw $H_d(\mathbf a)$ action is faithful in the stable range. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 The corner outside the stable range. For admissible $c$ outside the stable range, enlarge the pyramid as in [F4] until the stable range holds for the enlarged pyramid, with an idempotent $e$ selecting the added ground rows. The supported simple labels are exactly the contractible ones after deletion; the lowered tensor module is the original one on the supported blocks, and the graded first-centralizer argument identifies its image with the $e$-corner of the enlarged Hecke action. By [F3] the finite-dimensional algebras here have projective covers and their regular modules decompose into projective indecomposables; under the stable Morita equivalence the module $eM$ is a right progenerator precisely for the supporting central blocks, so its right annihilator is the sum of the complementary central blocks and the image is $fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ for the central idempotent $f$ of the supporting blocks. [F1, F3, F4, algebra, construct]

2.1 Centrality of $f$ and the status of the $e(\mathbf i)$. The individual generalized-eigenvalue idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$ are not central: the $S_d$-orbit sums of $e(\mathbf i)$ are the primitive central idempotents, so only orbit sums (and sums of such over supporting blocks) define two-sided corners. This is why $f$ is defined as a sum of entire central blocks. [F2, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Nonadmissible boundary. For nonadmissible $c$ the genuine image algebra exists and the tensor double centralizer holds by [F1], but the central-corner identification uses the admissible Morita equivalence and is not inferred here. [F1, step 1.2, given] ∎

items.title: Hecke induction and restriction functors on degenerate cyclotomic blocks
items.statement: For H(a) and its root-coset block decomposition, restriction e_i selects the last generalized x_(d+1) eigenvalue i after the tower inclusion; induction f_i is the corresponding B_(d+1)u tensor_(B_d)−. The degree/central-component idempotent u is the actual last-eigenvalue projector, not a claim that its corner equals the source algebra. These functors are exact, biadjoint and commute with ordinary *-duality; their Grothendieck operators are adjoint for the projective/module Hom pairing. Integral roots use the integer type-A indexing; nonintegral roots use their separate integer-coset chains. The full H(a) tower is obtained in sufficiently large admissible stable realizations; the image towers use the compatible projected tensor actions.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. The first d Casimir operators on T_(d+1)=T_d tensor V are those on T_d tensor1, so every zero image operator remains zero and the image tower map is well defined. Tensor adjunction gives π_d(GN)=Res π_(d+1)(N). The offStd kernel is stable under residue tensor operators by the actual16 highest projection and positivity of simple coefficients, so exact biadjoints descend to the quotient. Uniqueness of adjoints identifies their induction with B_(d+1)u tensor_(B_d)− and proves exactness/biadjunction. Finite admissible stable realizations cover every requested full Hecke block. The top PBW symmetric trace and the contravariant form on T identify πD with ordinary *-duality via the balanced evaluation map; two-term copresentations and projective presentations extend the identity from T to every object. Thus the functors commute with duality and the pairing adjunction follows. No unsupported Koszul grading or arbitrary corner equality is used. See Whittaker-quotient §7.

items.statement: For admissible c, the right Hecke action gives End_g(P_c tensor V^tensor d)^op=B_d, the image H_d(λ,c). On each central component it gives End_g(T_α)^op=B_α=f_α H_α(a) f_α. items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Hence End_g(T)^op=B_d, respecting the right-action opposite. Project central idempotents to obtain the component equalities. Stable injectivity and the outside-range central support follow from the preceding definition. This does not use false preservation of all projectives under Wh.

items.title: Higher-level Schur-Weyl double centralizer and full faithfulness on projectives
items.statement: The raw W_d and Hecke image B_d are mutual centralizers for every complex origin. For admissible origins, V_c^tensor d is a Morita progenerator and Hom_W(V_c^tensor d,−) is the equivalence W_d-mod→B_d-mod. The genuine Whittaker functor followed by this equivalence is the exact Schur Serre quotient killing offStd simples. It is fully faithful on all O projectives and on tiltings. The left adjoint is right exact and recovers add(T), not automatically all projectives. Stable range replaces B_d by H_d(a); otherwise the admissible-origin central-corner component B_d=fH_d(a)f is used.

The finite nonadmissible origin matrix and equal-charge rank-one adjoint witness show why the two extra hypotheses/conclusions must stay distinguished. items.title: Schur functor images of standard, simple, projective and tilting objects
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$. Let
$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ be the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Use the current category-O namespace:
$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,
$L(A)$ the category-O simple and $P(A)$ its projective cover, as in
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The source17 symbol $K(A)$ denotes our $L(A)$, not our costandard $K(A)$.
Write $\mathsf L(A):=\mathrm{Wh}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple
appearing in the Whittaker/Morita contract of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module
   $$S(A)=H_d(\mathbf a)\otimes_{H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}}\Bigl(\bigotimes_j \mathrm{ev}^*_{a_j}S^{\mu^{(j)}}\Bigr),\qquad a_j=c_j+q_j-n,$$
   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced
   along the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}=H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots
   \otimes H_{d_l}$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is
   simple, the modules $D(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, form a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,
   $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, where $d_{B,A}$ is the typed
   canonical-basis coefficient of the Fock-space dictionary; for $B\notin
   \mathrm{Std}$ the symbol $D(B)$ is not a Hecke simple. All interfaces are
   ungraded at parameter $1$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The admissible origin $c$, the tensor object $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, the Schur functor $\pi$, the standard and costandard objects $N(A),K(A)$, the simples $L(A)$, the projectives $P(A)$, and the Hecke image $B_d$.

[F1] In the actual category-O namespace the generalized standards are $M(A)=N(A)$, the simples are $L(A)$, projective covers are $P(A)$ and costandards are $\nabla(A)=K(A)$. These have the BGG reciprocity and standard/costandard/tilting flags of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]] and [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]. Composition multiplicities below are always taken against the simple $L(B)$; they are not standard-flag multiplicities against a costandard.

[F2] The Schur functor $\pi$ is exact, kills exactly the off-standard simples, recovers $\operatorname{add}(T)$ under $\pi^*\pi$, and is fully faithful on all projectives and on all tiltings; $T$ contains every standard-labelled projective-injective cover ([[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]], [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]]).

[F3] The filtered double centralizer identifies $B_d=\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the Schur quotient is the composite of the genuine Whittaker functor with the Morita equivalence; the stable range gives $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ ([[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]], [[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]], [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]).

[F4] The Fock-space dictionary: the canonical, dual-canonical and quasi-canonical bases of the higher-level Fock module carry the typed labels of simples, projectives and tiltings of the summand, and the coefficient $d_{B,A}(1)$ computes the corresponding multiplicity at parameter $1$ ([[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]).

[F5] The cyclotomic Hecke algebra has the bounded monomial basis and the evaluation homomorphisms $\mathrm{ev}_{a}\colon H_{d_j}(\mathbf a)\to\mathbb C[S_{d_j}]$ at the roots $a_j$ ([[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The standard $N(A)$, the costandard $K(A)$, the labels of $\mathrm{Std}$, and the corner data of the stable realization.

1.1 The Specht isomorphism. Choose a sufficiently large admissible stable realization in which the pyramid has $d$ distinct full ground rows; the row-torus weight idempotent $e_S$ of those rows is an element of the finite-W image, commuting with the Hecke action, and $e_SV_c^{\otimes d}$ has dimension $l^dd!$ with the words using the $d$ chosen rows as a basis, so evaluation at the regular vector identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ with $e_S(-)$. The corner operators are the row permutations together with $h(x_i)=e_S(-D^{(2)}_{r_i}+e_2(c)+e_1(c)+d-n-i+1)e_S$, where $D^{(2)}_{r_i}$ is the degree-two Gauss/path coefficient; on the canonical colour fibre of the finite Levi standard $V(A)$ this acts by $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ plus the within-column Jucys-Murphy sum, and the colour fibre is the tensor product of the column Specht modules $\bigotimes_jS^{\mu^{(j)}}$ by ordinary Schur-Weyl. Row permutations carry this fibre to every other colour fibre and span $e_SV(A)$, so dimension counting gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(A))\cong S(A)$, and by adjunction $\pi(N(A))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,N(A))\cong S(A)$. [F1, F3, F5, algebra, construct]

1.2 Tilting images. A tilting object has a standard flag and a costandard flag by [F1]; applying the exact functor $\pi$ to the standard flag expresses $\pi$ of the tilting with the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag coefficients, and the standard/socle polarity used for full faithfulness on tiltings shows that the quotient is fully faithful there. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Outside the stable range. If $q_l<d$ the admissible-origin construction enlarges the pyramid by adding full ground rows until $d$ rows are distinct; contractible labels restrict to the original pyramid and the corner $e_S$ detects exactly them, so the identification of step 1.1 descends to the original objects; this is the same enlargement used for the central corner and it does not change the Hecke roots. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 The simple images. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ exactness of $\pi$ and the quotient description of [F2] give $\pi(L(A))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))=D(A)$, and the cosocle of the Specht module $S(A)=\pi(N(A))$ is $D(A)$ by the canonical highest-vector argument; since $\pi$ kills exactly the off-standard simples, $D(A)=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$, and the standard labels give all distinct simples of $B_d$ because every Hecke simple is a composition factor of some $S(A)$ and distinct standard labels give non-isomorphic $D(A)$. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Projective images. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the cover $P(A)$ lies in $\operatorname{add}(T)$ by [F2]; hence $\pi(P(A))$ is a direct summand of $\pi(T)=B_d$, so it is projective, and its head is $D(A)$ by exactness, which makes it the projective cover $Y(A)$ of $D(A)$; the elementary identity $\pi^*\pi\cong\mathrm{id}$ on $\operatorname{add}(T)$ then gives $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$. For off-standard labels the image $\pi(P(A))$ is the genuine image of an ambient projective and is not claimed to be projective. [F2, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 Multiplicities. Since $\pi$ is exact and its kernel is generated by the off-standard simples, the composition multiplicities of $S(A)=\pi(N(A))$ are the multiplicities of the simple $L(B)$ in $N(A)$ for $B\in\mathrm{Std}$; by the Fock-space dictionary [F4] the typed coefficient of the dual-canonical/canonical pairing equals $d_{B,A}(1)$, so $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$; for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}$ the module $D(B)$ is zero and is not a simple Hecke label. All the identifications above are ungraded and taken at parameter $1$. [F2, F4, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The intrinsic definition of $S(A)$ by parabolic induction replaces the faulty direct $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak p}$ identification of the source with the corner/regular-vector computation: the canonical colour fibre is only one of several fibres of $e_SV(A)$, and the corner operators supply the correct extension.
- The proof deliberately separates the stable-range corner computation (steps 1.1 and 2.1) from the exact-quotient consequences (steps 1.2, 2.2, 3.1 and 4.1); the latter only use exactness, the kernel description and the Fock dictionary, so they are insensitive to the choice of stable realization.

items.title: Category-O translation intertwines residue induction and restriction
items.statement: There are natural isomorphisms f_i^H π≅π f_i^O and e_i^H π≅π e_i^O, compatible with residue projectors, units/counits and ordinary restricted/*-dualities. Consequently the ungraded Grothendieck operators at parameter1 agree and the Schur quotient is a module map. Category O uses the genuine typed coset realization for admissible nonintegral origins, not an unqualified integer block. This statement preserves the actual residue/standard filtrations; an unspecified graded parity or Koszul lift is not asserted by these ungraded suppliers.

The kernel-stable exact quotient descends the biadjoint O translations, so uniqueness of left/right adjoints gives induction, with the actual units and counits. items.title: The degenerate affine Hecke relations on two tensor factors
items.statement: For gl_2, M=V and d=2, let P_ab permute factors a,b of V^tensor3. Then x_1=P_01, s_1=P_12 and x_2=P_02+P_12. Their eight-by-eight tensor-basis matrices satisfy s_1²=1, [x_1,x_2]=0, s_1 x_2−x_1 s_1=1 and x_2 s_1−s_1 x_1=1. For v_1 tensor v_2 tensor v_1, x_1 s_1 sends it to v_1 tensor v_1 tensor v_2, while s_1 x_2 sends it to the sum of that vector and the original. The commutator [s_1,x_2] is not literally1; the affine cross relation has the distinct x_1 on its other side.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Write each P_ab as its permutation of the eight binary words. Products of the three transpositions verify both affine relations. Expand [P_01,P_02+P_12]; the two oriented three-cycles cancel. Enumerate the basis words to check the displayed example and all matrix entries; this finite example tests the normalization, not the general proof.

items.title: A level-two cyclotomic polynomial from the highest-weight filtration
items.statement: Take source-ordered row lengths p=(1,2), q=(2,1), N=3, n=2, c=(0,0). Number boxes down columns:1=(1,1),2=(2,1),3=(2,2). Thus e=E23 and x_1 on V is E23+diag(0,0,−1). Its eigenvalue0 has multiplicity2 and eigenvalue−1 has multiplicity1; the −1 eigenspace is C(v_3−v_2). Its minimal polynomial is x(x+1), with roots a=(0,−1), Λ=Λ_0+Λ_−1. For every d≥1 the raw tensor x_1 still has exactly this minimal polynomial by the column-filtration and leading-string argument. H_d(Λ) has dimension2^d d!. At d=1 its image splits the two stated eigenspaces.

items.title: A Hecke action alone does not imply the double centralizer property
items.statement: Let $M=\mathbb C^2$ be the trivial $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$-module, $V=\mathbb C^2$ the natural module and $d=1$. The Arakawa-Suzuki construction provides an action of $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$ on $M\otimes V\cong\mathbb C^4$ commuting with $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, but here $x_1=\Omega^{M,V}=0$, so the action is the evaluation action $x_1\mapsto0$ and $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(\mathbb C^4)=M_4(\mathbb C)$. On the other hand the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ in $\mathrm{End}(M\otimes V)$ is the subalgebra $1_{\mathbb C^2}\otimes M_2(\mathbb C)$, of dimension $4$. Hence the equality $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=\mathrm{End}_{H_d}(M\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ fails by a factor of $4$ in dimension, even though the Hecke action is genuine, commutes with $\mathfrak g$, and is natural in $M$. The other equality also fails: $\psi(H_1)=\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}\subsetneq\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(M\otimes V)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\otimes1$, of dimension $4$. The hypothesis that is missing is the truncated/deformed setup: the double centralizer theorem applies to the finite-W-algebra tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ over the pyramid (equivalently to $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ with the truncated polynomial algebra $C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$), where the Hecke action is the cyclotomic quotient action and the algebra of the opposite side is the finite W-algebra, not $U(\mathfrak g)$.
items.strategy: Compute $x_1$ on $M\otimes V$: the Casimir tensor has its first tensor factor acting on the trivial module $M$, so $x_1=0$; this is a legitimate instance of the Arakawa-Suzuki action, since the construction assigns an $H_d$-action to every $\mathfrak g$-module $M$. Compute the two centralizers in the bases $\{u_a\otimes v_b\}$: $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)$ is all of $M_4$ because $H_1$ acts by scalars, while $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=1\otimes M_2$ has dimension $4$; the other centralizer is $M_2\otimes1$ versus $\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}$. Hence both double centralizer equalities fail. This is not a counterexample to the higher-level Schur-Weyl theorem: it shows that the theorem needs the finite-W-algebra deformation/truncation hypotheses, and that a mere commuting Hecke action on an arbitrary tensor module is insufficient.

items.title: Vust's double centralizer in a small stable range
items.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$, so $n=2$, $l=1$, $q_1=2$, $N=2$, $e=0$, all boxes in one column and the grading is concentrated in degree $0$: $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g^e=\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $\mathfrak m=0$, $C_1[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1,\dots,x_d)=\mathbb C$, and $C_1[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]=\mathbb C[S_d]$. Verify Vust's double centralizer for $d=1,2$, which is the stable range for this $\lambda$ (at least $d$ parts equal to $l=1$ holds for $d\le2$). For $d=1$: $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V)=\mathbb C\cdot1=\psi_1(\mathbb C[S_1])$ and $\varphi_1(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V)$, as $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)\to\mathrm{End}(V)$ is surjective. For $d=2$: $V^{\otimes2}=S^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$, $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes2})=2=\dim\mathbb C[S_2]$ with $\psi_2$ injective, and $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb C[S_2]}(V^{\otimes2})=\dim\mathrm{End}(S^2V)+\dim\mathrm{End}(\Lambda^2V)=9+1=10=\dim\varphi_2(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))$; check the two decompositions explicitly (the flip acts as $+1$ on $S^2V$ and $-1$ on $\Lambda^2V$, and the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ is exactly the block-diagonal algebra of the two isotypic components).
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. One column has no left-neighbour boxes, so e=0, not E12. Then g^e=gl_2, m=0 and the truncated variables vanish. For d=1 matrix units span End V. For d=2 compute the symmetric and alternating tensor bases; the flip eigenvalues are ±1 and ordinary complete reducibility gives their full9+1 endomorphism blocks. Both irreducible constituents occur, so C[S_2] acts injectively. These checks realize the full Vust theorem in its actual stable range.

items.title: A block idempotent corner outside the stable range
items.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$ (so $l=1$, two parts equal to $1$) and $d=3$: the stable range fails, because at least $3$ parts of $\lambda$ equal to $1$ is false. Here $H_3(\Lambda)=\mathbb C[S_3]$ (level $l=1$), of dimension $6$, while the image $H_3(\lambda,c)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}$, $V=\mathbb C^2$, has dimension $5$: for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $V^{\otimes3}=L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$, so $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ has dimension $1+4=5$, and it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Under the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ (trivial, sign and standard blocks), the map to $\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ kills exactly the sign block; hence $H_3(\lambda,c)\cong f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ with $f$ the central idempotent of the trivial and standard blocks, and $f$ is the block idempotent corner of the Definition. Verify: $\dim f\mathbb C[S_3]f=1+4=5$, the map $\mathbb C[S_3]\twoheadrightarrow f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ is multiplication by $f$, and the antisymmetrizer $a=\sum_{w\in S_3}\mathrm{sgn}(w)w$ spans the kernel of the action on $V^{\otimes3}$ because $\Lambda^3V=0$ for $\dim V=2$.
items.strategy: Decompose $V^{\otimes3}$ for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ by the classical Schur-Weyl rule: the partitions of $3$ with at most $2$ rows are $(3)$ and $(2,1)$, so $V^{\otimes3}\cong L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$; hence $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})\cong\mathbb C\times M_2$, of dimension $5$, and by Schur-Weyl duality it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Compare with the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2$: the sign block acts on $V^{\otimes3}$ by zero because the sign representation does not occur in $V^{\otimes3}$ (equivalently $\Lambda^3V=0$), so the kernel is the sign block and the image is the corner of the other two blocks. The dimension count and the corner identification verify the general statement of the preceding Definition in the smallest non-stable case.
